vSphere Kubernetes Service 3.6.1+v1.35
Release Snapshot
vSphere Kubernetes Service 3.6.1 is generally available for use with vSphere 9.x and vSphere 8.x.
Name Release Date
vSphere Kubernetes Service 3.6.1+v1.35 13-April-2026
VMware by Broadcom 32

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
What's New
• VKS 3.6.1 includes a CAPI bump for upstream enhancements and security fixes. CAPI bump includes a fix to mitigate
an upstream kube-apiserver issue.
What's New on VKS 3.6.1 with VCF 9.1
• Support for multi-network in VKS
VKS multi-network support introduces the ability to provision worker nodes with a dedicated secondary network
interface and pods with additional interfaces managed by Antrea CNI. This capability enables the isolation of
management traffic from high-demand data traffic, such as NFS storage or database replication. By supporting SR-
IOV for near-wire-speed performance, VKS now provides the hardware-aware networking required for demanding
enterprise workloads and connects VKS Pods to external multicast traffic through VPC VLAN Extension subnets.
• Run Antrea CNI in hybrid encapsulation mode on VKS
Antrea CNI can run in Hybrid mode, which turns off encapsulation for inter-node Pod-to-Pod and Pod-to-Service traffic
when belonging to the same subnet for significant performance gain, with up to 40% observed in TCP transactions
and latency related metrics. This provides a more efficient datapath with reduced processing cost on Linux Nodes
and improved throughput for common intra-cluster traffic patterns. Hybrid mode also preserves full compatibility with
all major Antrea features supported in encapsulation mode - such as AntreaProxy, Egress, AntreaNetworkPolicy,
NodePortLocal, AntreaProxy, Multicast, and more.
• More VKS clusters per Supervisor
Enhanced validated configuration maximums enabling a 2.5x increase in the number of clusters with up to 500 VKS
clusters and up to 4000 total VKS clusters nodes on a given Supervisor. Platform administrators do not have to deploy
multiple supervisors when they have to scale their deployments horizontally. This reduces the operational overhead
managing additional Supervisors for the platform administrators. This means VCF 9.1 with VKS 3.6 will support greater
flexibility and scalability for large scale Kubernetes deployments on vSphere Kubernetes Service. Please refer to the
configmax.broadcom.com site for the updated configuration maximum numbers.
• Reduced time to deploy and upgrade VKS clusters with VM Fast Deploy
Improved efficiency allows for accelerated creation and upgrade of VKS clusters by significantly decreasing the time
needed to provision each individual VM. Deploying VKS cluster control plane and worker nodes includes provisioning a
number of VMs in the process. The time required to provision all these VMs adds to the time required to spin up a new
VKS cluster. In a large production environment, cluster creation and upgrades are often happening at massive scale
impacting the efficiency and time taken to bring up these clusters to the Ready state. VKS 3.6 now has implemented a
more efficient approach to provision Virtual machines. Users will experience a significant improvement in efficiency and
speed at which the clusters are created and upgraded. Under ideal lab conditions, a VKS cluster with 100 worker node
was created in 4 minutes (70% improvement) and upgrade took about 30 minutes (a 85% improvement) with the VM
Fast Deploy approach.
• Support for EncryptionClass
EncryptionClass support introduces a sophisticated layer of multi-tenancy in VKS when working with VCF Automation,
allowing you to assign unique encryption keys to specific tenants for true data isolation. By leveraging this integration,
infrastructure admins can delegate security ownership, enabling separate business units to manage their own
cryptographic boundaries within a shared VCF-A environment. This ensures that while the underlying infrastructure is
unified, the data remains cryptographically siloed, allowing each tenant to meet their specific compliance mandates
through independent key management and life cycle control.
• Node pool auto placement
With this release, the failureDomain parameter is now optional, allowing the VKS placement to automatically manage
resource distribution. To guarantee high availability by default, the system intelligently distributes node pools across
separate zones during cluster creation. It ensures that all VMs within a specific node pool remain localized within a
single zone. Furthermore, the placement logic operates on a best-effort basis to distribute these VMs across distinct
physical hosts, providing an additional layer of hardware redundancy and ensuring robust cluster resilience without
requiring manual intervention.
• Manage CNI add-ons via new add-on management APIs
VKS 3.6.1 introduces the ability to utilize custom CNI solutions through the VKS Add-on Framework, giving platform
engineers the freedom to standardize on the networking stack that best fits their operational requirements.
VMware by Broadcom 33

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
– Strategic CNI Foundation (Antrea): VMware Antrea remains the strategic, default CNI for VKS. It provides an out-
of-the-box, enterprise-grade networking and security foundation with deep integration into the VCF management
plane.
– Validated CNI Options (Cilium): For workloads requiring specialized eBPF-based networking and observability,
Cilium is now available as a validated Standard Package. This allows customers to leverage Cilium’s advanced load
balancing and transparent encryption while maintaining the lifecycle benefits of the VKS Add-on Service.
• Hierarchical configuration of trusted CA certificates
Provides enhanced flexibility for managing trusted CA certificates across your Kubernetes infrastructure. You can
now configure CA certificates at the Supervisor, Supervisor Namespace, or individual cluster level, ensuring that
all existing and newly created workload clusters automatically inherit and trust the specified certificates. Notably,
adding or updating a namespace-scoped CA certificate will not trigger a rolling update of existing clusters, allowing for
seamless security configuration changes without service disruption.
• Prevent fleet wide rollouts when changes to Fleet Depot Service and registries are made
Enables Admins to activate the Software Depot Service during a VCF 9.1 upgrade without triggering a disruptive fleet-
wide rollout of existing Kubernetes clusters. This ensures that critical platform operations, such as updating the default
infrastructure registry, remain transparent and impact-free for your running workloads.
• Package management with Harbor endpoint
Simplified how VKS clusters consume OCI objects from the Harbor Service. By adding the Harbor endpoint to the
hosts file on each cluster node, both new and existing clusters can reliably resolve depot.kube-system.svc to the
Harbor Load Balancer IP. This enhancement ensures a consistent experience for pulling system and add-on package
images without requiring complex DNS configurations.
Fixed Issues
Clusters configured with maxPods > 110 on VKS 3.6.0 experience infinite control plane rollouts.
Issue has been fixed in this release
Known Issues
(VCF 9.1) Windows nodes in VKS clusters fail to start and remain in a False state when container registry
configurations are applied
On VCF 9.1, and are automatically applied to the Supervisor if a
ClusterRegistryConfig RegistryConfig
container registry or regional Harbor is registered. When this happens, Windows nodes with a Kubernetes release version
earlier than 1.35.0 get stuck during bootstrapping. This occurs because the service fails to start due to
containerd
an empty default runtime name in its configuration. This issue can affect both new (greenfield) and existing (brownfield)
environments.
Workaround: Upgrade VKS to 3.6.2. For existing clusters, wait approximately 60 minutes for the machine health check
to trigger an automatic rollout. Alternatively, you can manually annotate the machines with
cluster.x-k8s.io/
to trigger an immediate remediation.
remediate-machine
(VCF 9.1) VKS cluster enters a False state when a single-zone environment is transitioned to a multi-zone
topology
This issue might occur after you upgrade to VCF 9.1 and VKS 3.6. If a VKS cluster was initially deployed in a single-
zone environment using an Immediate binding StorageClass and then more zones are added to its namespace, the
cluster status is marked as False. Any attempt to update the cluster configuration results in a validation error stating that a
WaitForFirstConsumer (late-binding) StorageClass is required for multi-zone environments.
Workaround: Update the StorageClass for the node pools to use WaitForFirstConsumer (late-binding) binding mode.
(VCF 9.1) Cluster status becomes False after you upgrade to VKS 3.6 and VCF 9.1
In VKS 3.6 and VCF 9.1, clusters without a defined failureDomain require a StorageClass using WaitForFirstConsumer
binding mode. If you previously deployed a cluster using Immediate binding mode and the namespace was later migrated
from a single-zone to a multi-zone setup, the cluster status becomes False after the upgrade.
You might observe errors including the following:
failed to call extension handler "generate-
.
patches.runtime-extension"
Workaround:
VMware by Broadcom 34

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
Use one of the following methods:
• To avoid this issue, before upgrading to VKS 3.6 and VCF 9.1, explicitly add a failureDomain to each node pool.
• To restore the cluster status after upgrading to VKS 3.6 and VCF 9.1, add a failureDomain to each node pool.
Alternatively, you can switch the StorageClass to a version that uses WaitForFirstConsumer binding, typically indicated
by a -latebinding suffix.
Note: Both actions will trigger a rolling update of the affected node pools.
(VCF 9.1) Automatic rolling update of VKS clusters occurs after you upgrade VCF along with Supervisor to 9.1
with regional Harbor deployed
When you upgrade VCF or Supervisor to version 9.1 in environments where regional Harbor is deployed, all VKS clusters
undergo an automatic rolling update. This happens because clusters must rotate their nodes to adopt the new certificates
and DNS entries required by the regional Harbor infrastructure. This issue affects environments where the VKS has been
upgraded to 3.6.1, but the individual cluster nodes have not yet been rolled out.
Workaround: To avoid an unplanned rolling update, before upgrade to VCF 9.1, perform the following steps:
1. Upgrade the VKS to version 3.6.1 or later.
2. Retire any legacy (v1alpha3) clusters.
For details, see Retire TanzuKubernetesCluster Resources.
3. Upgrade all VKS clusters to use ClusterClass 3.6.0 or later to ensure all nodes adopt the updated machine-agent.
(VCF 9.1) VKS clusters using ClusterClass 3.1.0 cannot consume packages from a regional Harbor
In VCF 9.1, the default AddonRepository that is configured with a regional Harbor URL (Fleet Depot Service) cannot be
resolved by VKS clusters that were deployed using ClusterClass 3.1.0 . As a result, VKS standard packages cannot be
installed and used from the regional Harbor repository.
Workaround:
• Upgrade the cluster to use ClusterClass 3.2.0 or later.
• Alternatively, you can update the AddonRepositoryInstall to use a public URL or a functional private registry URL.

VKS control plane nodes are stuck in NotReady state after trust configuration for a Cluster is updated
Steps to Reproduce:
• Create a cluster with ClusterClass version builtin-generic-v3.6.0
• After the Cluster has transitioned to be Available, update the osConfiguration variable at the Cluster level or as a
control plane override to add a new cert to the trusted certs for the Cluster. Refer to the variable documentation here,
to learn more about how to set up trusted certs for an individual Cluster.
• This should propagate the trust configuration to the VKS Cluster.
• The Cluster displaying this issue would have their Available condition set to False, which can also shows up in the
kubectl get cluster command's output.
Workaround
• Once the container is identified, identify the orphaned process using `ps -a` on the node. Once the orphaned process
is isolated, run `kill -9 PID` to clean up the orphaned process.
• Wait for containerd to automatically restart the failing container, ensure the STATE of the container is RUNNING using
the ` ` command
crictl ps -a

Release Snapshot

Name Release Date
vSphere Kubernetes Service 3.6.0+v1.35 11-February-2026
What's New
Lifecycle & Upgrades
• Support for Kubernetes 1.35 - VKS 3.6 introduces compatibility for vSphere Kubernetes release 1.35. To upgrade
your VKS clusters to v1.35, you must upgrade the VKS version to VKS 3.6. VKr 1.35 will be supported for a period of
24 months. Refer to the Product Lifecycle page for the updated support period of vSphere Kubernetes releases.
VMware by Broadcom 37

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
• Standard Packages - The default embedded in VKS 3.6 is the Standard package
AddonRepository
release v3.6.0+20260211. After upgrading to VKS 3.6, the default for standard
AddonRepositoryInstall
packages will automatically be switched to 3.6.0+20260211 release. To skip auto-update, use the annotation
addons.kubernetes.vmware.com/skip-vks-managed-addon-repository-update. Refer to the Product
documentation.
• Support for RHEL based Nodes - VKS 3.6 introduces support for RHEL based custom node OS images. You can
now configure VKS Clusters to run on RHEL Based nodes. You can use the new imagebaker tool (replacing Image
Builder) to build custom node images for RHEL
: VKS provides full Enterprise support for built-in Photon OS and Ubuntu node images. These images are
Note
bundled with the VCF subscription and do not require additional OS licensing. However, for Red Hat Enterprise Linux
(RHEL) and Windows nodes, the following policies apply-
– Licensing: Users must bring their own valid subscriptions for RHEL and Windows OS (BYO Licensing).
– VKS Support Scope: Support for Custom nodes is limited to the platform’s image generation capabilities (via
ImageBaker). Any OS related issue for RHEL and Windows must be taken up with the respective OS vendors.
• ImageBaker integrated with VCF CLI - VKS 3.6 introduces integration of Image Baker with VCF CLI , to help
streamline the creation of custom node OS images.
– Capabilities: ImageBaker helps build custom node images for Photon OS, Ubuntu, Windows, and RHEL.
– Version Support: Supports Kubernetes v1.35 and future patch releases for earlier minor versions.
– Operational Efficiency: Unlike its predecessor, Image Baker is a standalone tool that operates independently of
vCenter, significantly reducing infrastructure requirements for image generation.
– Legacy Support: The existing Image Builder tool remains supported for building images for Kubernetes v1.34 and
earlier.
• Guardrails to prevent Cluster lifecycle failures due to misconfigured policy tools - VKS 3.6 introduces
pre-upgrade checks to detect misconfigured software such as Admission Webhooks, in addition to the existing
misconfigured Pod Disruption Budgets (PDBs) check that can block the cluster upgrade process. Previously, these
configurations could cause the upgrades to stall or fail without a clear indication of the root cause. To address this, the
SystemChecksSucceeded has been expanded and will now include specific details of the misconfigured webhooks
and dry-runs failures. This significantly enhances the cluster stability and provides a more reliable and predictable
upgrade path.
Configuration & Security
• New builtin-generic-v3.6.0 ClusterClass - VKS 3.6 supports builtin-generic-v3.6.0 ClusterClass which introduces
additional ClusterClass variables for you to configure your VKS cluster.
• Support for Customized Linux Nodes Performance profiles - VKS 3.6 now enables the configuration of low-
level system tunables through the introduction of TuneD profiles as Custom Resources in the Supervisor Cluster.
This feature allows advanced users to fine-tune critical kernel parameters including CPU, memory management,
networking, block device, and I/O scheduling- to meet the demands of high performance applications. To help you get
started, VKS includes a pre-configured TuneD profile optimized for general purpose workloads.
• Support for AppArmor Profiles - VKS 3.6 introduces a native, declarative orchestration for AppArmor, enabling
Mandatory Access Control (MAC) management at scale across diverse nodepools (Photon OS and Ubuntu nodes).
This eliminates the need for manual per-node configuration-a process that is operationally intensive and fails to
survive node restarts or lifecycle updates. VKS now ensures security policies are automatically synchronized and
persistent across all the worker nodes. This allows administrators to enforce a uniform security baseline across the
entire cluster from a single, centralized control plane.
• Select the Container Networking Interface (CNI) during Cluster Creation - With VKS 3.6, when creating a Cluster
using the vSphere Kubernetes version 1.35, you can now select the CNI using the ClusterClass
bootstrapAddons
variable. Selecting a CNI via the workflow is no longer supported for VKr 1.35+. Antrea CNI will
ClusterBootstrap
continue to be enabled by default if no CNI is explicitly selected. Status of the CNI Addon in VKr 1.35 Clusters can be
viewed via VCF Automation 9.0.1 and later.
• Simplified CNI Configuration via Addon Framework - VKS introduces a more modular approach to managing
Container Network Interface (CNI) configurations. CNI configurations (such as Antrea and Calico) are now managed
through the VKS Addon Framework using the custom resource. This replaces the previous
AddonConfig
method for version 1.35 and later. Users can now pre-configure CNI settings before cluster
ClusterBootstrap
creation or modify them post-deployment by simply updating the resource in the cluster namespace.
AddonConfig
VMware by Broadcom 38

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
For customers upgrading existing VKS clusters to VKr 1.35, VKS will migrate the existing CNI configuration resources
( , ) to the new framework.
AntreaConfig CalicoConfig
• Common interface across all supported node OS to configure inbound firewall rules - VKS 3.6 introduces
a consistent, OS-agnostic API that allows Cluster administrators to specify inbound firewall rules during the cluster
creation. This eliminates the need to manage disparate tools-such as iptables for Linux, or netsh for Windows - to
secure the environment. Administrators can now define security policies (source IPs, CIDR blocks, protocol and ports),
through a single interface applied to all the supported operating systems. This also allows for the configuration of
additional port ranges and protocols on node interfaces beyond the standard Kubernetes high node port ranges. This
approach is specifically valuable for clusters with mixed nodepools, significantly reducing the operational complexity
and risk of misconfiguration across diverse nodepools.
• Support for Late-Binding Storage Class as the Cluster default - VKS 3.6 introduces the capability to designate
storage classes with WaitForFirstConsumer (WFFC)-commonly referred to as the late-binding as the cluster
default. This is designed to address the common challenge of cross-zone mounting failures in multi-zone (Multi-AZ)
environments. By delaying the volume creation until a pod is scheduled to a specific node, VKS guarantees that
storage is physically provisioned in the same availability zone as the compute resource. This eliminates the need for
administrators to manually specify zone-aware storage for every workload, ensuring high availability by default. To
enable this, users simply append the -latebinding suffix to the default configuration.
StorageClass
Others
• VKS Support Bundle tool enhancements - The VKS Support Bundle tool has been updated in version 3.6 to
streamline diagnostic data collection and improve security delegation. VKS Cluster users can now generate support
bundles independently, without requiring elevated vCenter SSO Administrator permissions. By removing the
dependency on vSphere Administrators, cluster users can instantly initiate log collection during critical troubleshooting
windows.
Fixed Issues
• Bootstrap of nodes has been made more robust by retrying downloads of configuration components on first boot on
Linux

clusters are deleted.

• Introduced a option for addon upgrades, allowing upgrades to proceed even when the addon status is not
--force
. Note: It does not apply to core addons yet
Ready=True

• Cluster creation failure after certificate rotation for runtime extensions pod
• Allow supervisor SSO users to safely trigger machine remediation via the cluster.x-k8s.io/remediate-machine label
• Fix issue where support bundle wrongly marks Windows VMs in some cases
• VKS 3.6.0 introduces an admission webhook to manage configurations involving the maximumDBSizeGiB variable
(introduced in VKS v3.5.0) and manual /var/lib/etcd volume mounts. For existing clusters created prior to 3.5.0, a
warning is now issued if a manual /var/lib/etcd mount is detected, allowing them to remain in a legacy state. For new
clusters, the validation webhook will issue a warning when manual /var/lib/etcd mount is used. A validation error will
now block any configuration that attempts to define a manual mount alongside the maximumDBSizeGiB variable, as
these provisioning methods are mutually exclusive.

• KB: https://knowledge.broadcom.com/external/article?articleNumber=432638
VKS control plane nodes are stuck in NotReady state after trust configuration for a Cluster is updated
Steps to Reproduce:
• Create a cluster with ClusterClass version builtin-generic-v3.6.0
• After the Cluster has transitioned to be Available, update the osConfiguration variable at the Cluster level or as a
control plane override to add a new cert to the trusted certs for the Cluster. Refer to the variable documentation here,
to learn more about how to set up trusted certs for an individual Cluster.
• This should propagate the trust configuration to the VKS Cluster.
• The Cluster displaying this issue would have their Available condition set to False, which can also shows up in the
kubectl get cluster command's output.
Workaround
• Once the container is identified, identify the orphaned process using `ps -a` on the node. Once the orphaned process
is isolated, run `kill -9 PID` to clean up the orphaned process.
• Wait for containerd to automatically restart the failing container, ensure the STATE of the container is RUNNING using
the ` ` command
crictl ps -a
Clusters created with VKS v3.4.0 or earlier will see an intermittent control plane provisioned and deleted during
VKr version upgrades.
After VKS upgrades from v3.4.x or below, existing clusters triggering a Kubernetes version upgrade and/or ClusterClass
version update, will observe the first newer control plane machine's Up-To-Date condition be marked as False almost
immediately after it starts to be provisioned. This means that the first control plane machine will be rolled out twice during
the upgrade.
This machine eventually moves to the Ready state and is instantly deleted to be replaced by another up-to-date control
place machine. The rollout of the cluster progresses successfully after.
Steps to reproduce:
1. Create a cluster using VKS v3.4.1 (or below) using any of the shipped ClusterClass versions, say, builtin-generic-
v3.4.0
2. Upgrade VKS to version v3.6.0
3. Update the VKr version in use by the Cluster by updating the spec.topology.version field.
No manual intervention is necessary, the first newer control plane machine gets deleted and recreated. The rest of the
Cluster upgrade progresses successfully.
Creating a VKS cluster fails due to Velero webhook failures
VMware by Broadcom 40

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
When creating a VKS cluster, the process fails, and you observe the following error:
failed to create
or update VirtualMachine: Internal error occurred: failed calling webhook
"cbt.mutate.virtualmachine"
The Velero vSphere Operator webhook monitors VM creation for VKS clusters and enables the Changed Block Tracking
(CBT) flag on the VM Custom Resource (CR) if required. If the Velero vSphere Operator webhook is unavailable, cluster
creation fails with the error mentioned above.
Workaround: Identify the cause of the webhook failure by inspecting the Velero vSphere Operator logs.
Rollout of nodes when using Harbor Supervisor Service with custom certificates
When using VKS alongside Harbor Supervisor Service configured with a custom certificate, Clusters on ClusterClasses
builtin-generic-v3.2.0, or builtin-generic-v3.3.0, or builtin-generic-v3.4.0, may undergo a node rollout post upgrade. This
happens because the ordering of trusted certificates has now been made deterministic such that subsequent reconciles of
the Cluster by VKS will always add the same certificate with the same consistent ordering. This is a one time rollout and
existing clusters should not undergo any such automatic rollouts in the future. This issue is observed only when using a
Harbor supervisor version < 2.11.2+vmware.1-tkg.2.
Either use the KB article to patch your current service to fix the labeling of secrets or consider upgrading Harbor
Supervisor Service to a version >=2.11.2. Both these workarounds will initiate a rollout on all existing Clusters. This issue
is observed only when using a Harbor supervisor version < 2.11.2+vmware.1-tkg.2.
VKS 3.5.0 and VKS 3.6.0 are not compatible with Data Services Manager 9.0.0 and 9.0.1.
Upgrading VKS to version 3.5.0 or VKS 3.6.0 will cause Data Services Manager versions 9.0.0 and 9.0.1 to become
inoperable. Refer to the interoperability matrix for more details.
Workaround: N/A
Resolution: Customers using DSM 9.0.0 and DSM 9.0.1 are advised not to upgrade to VKS 3.5.0 /or VKS 3.6.0 due to
known incompatibility.
Automatic Control Plane Roll-out when using Custom ClusterClass post upgrade to VKS v3.5 and higher
Existing VKS clusters created with a custom Class (CC) using the builtin-generic-v3.4.0 class will experience an automatic
rollout of their control plane nodes after upgrading to VKS 3.5.0.
Note: This unscheduled rollout only affects the control plane nodes, and workloads running on the cluster should remain
unaffected
Workaround:
There is no workaround available for this issue, as it stems from an incorrect inference of the base version of the custom
CC (in this case, 3.4.0).
Adding a content library to the supervisor with a duplicate KR version template (matching the cluster's KR
version) can cause the VKS cluster to enter a false state.
The cluster status will report "False" for the TopologyReconciled condition, with the message: "error computing the desired
state of the Cluster topology: failed to apply patches: failed to generate patches for patch "default": failed to call extension
handler "generate-patches.runtime-extension": got failure response."
Note: This condition does not impact the runtime availability of existing nodes, so current workloads on the cluster will
continue to run. It only affects future reconciliation and updates.
Workaround:
1. Delete the conflicting OS template from the newly added content library.
OR
2. Update the cluster's "run.tanzu.vmware.com/resolve-os-image" annotation with the content library ID.

About the vSphere Kubernetes Service 3.5 Release Notes
vSphere Kubernetes Service (VKS) provides components for provisioning and managing the lifecycle of Kubernetes
clusters in the vSphere Supervisor environment.
These release notes provide details for each VKS release. Refer to the Managing vSphere Kubernetes Service with
vSphere Supervisor documentation for usage information.
Versioning and Upgrades
vSphere Kubernetes Service (VKS) 3.5.x point releases do not introduce a new or different ClusterClass. They deliver the
same base 3.5.0 ClusterClass, bundled with cumulative bug fixes and underlying improvements.
To ensure cluster stability and receive critical bug fixes, always upgrade to the latest available point release. For the core
requirements, refer back to the baseline VKS 3.5.0+v1.34.
Prerequisites for VKS 3.5 Upgrade
• vCenter and Supervisor Kubernetes version - VKS 3.5 requires Supervisor Kubernetes version 1.30 or later.
Supervisor Kubernetes version 1.30 is available with vCenter 9.0 and vCenter 8.0 Update 3g and above. You must
upgrade the Supervisor Kubernetes version in vCenter to at least version 1.30. Refer to the interoperability matrix for
more details.
• VKr Version - VKS 3.5 drops compatibility for VKr v1.29 and v1.30. Before upgrading to VKS 3.5, you must ensure all
your VKS Clusters are running at least on VKr 1.31.
• VKS version - To upgrade to VKS 3.5 directly, the VKS version installed on the Supervisor must be at least VKS 3.2.
Refer to the upgrade path tool in the interoperability matrix for more details.
• Support for VKr 1.34. This release adds support for VKr version 1.34 and drops the compatibility for VKr 1.29 and
v1.30. To upgrade to vSphere Kubernetes Service 3.5.0, all vSphere Kubernetes Service (VKS) clusters must be
running VKr 1.31 or higher. Refer to the interoperability matrix for more details.
Deprecation Announcements in VKS 3.5
• Cluster API v1beta1 API Version - Cluster API v1beta1 version is now deprecated and will be removed in upcoming
VKS releases. See upstream Cluster API Issue #11920 for more details.
• builtin-generic-v3.4.0 ClusterClass - With the release of VKS 3.5, the ClusterClass
builtin-generic-v3.5.0
is introduced and recommended for use. Existing clusters must rebase to as a part of,
builtin-generic-v3.5.0
or prior to, any upgrade to Kubernetes v1.34 or later. Additionally, the ClusterClass is
builtin-generic-v3.4.0
considered deprecated and will be removed in future releases.

Rollout of nodes when using Harbor Supervisor Service with custom certificates
When using VKS alongside Harbor Supervisor Service configured with a custom certificate, Clusters on ClusterClasses
builtin-generic-v3.2.0, or builtin-generic-v3.3.0, or builtin-generic-v3.4.0, may undergo anode rollout post upgrade. This
happens because the ordering of trusted certificates has now been made deterministic such that subsequent reconciles of
the Cluster by VKS will always add the same certificate with the same consistent ordering. This is a one time rollout and
existing clusters should not undergo any such automatic rollouts in the future. This issue is observed only when using a
Harbor supervisor version < 2.11.2+vmware.1-tkg.2.
Either use the KB article to patch your current service to fix the labeling of secrets or consider upgrading to a version
>=2.11.2. Both these workarounds will initiate a rollout on all existing TKCs. This issue is observed only when using a
Harbor supervisor version < 2.11.2+vmware.1-tkg.2.
An error will occur if the /var/lib/etcd volume mount and maximumDBSizeGiB are defined during cluster creation
or updates..
Clusters that retain a manual /var/lib/etcd volume mount after upgrading to VKS 3.5.0 will continue operating in a legacy
configuration and will not benefit from the new automated ETCD volume provisioning and quota management introduced
with the maximumDBSizeGiB variable.
• Edit the Cluster object and remove any user-defined volume mounts that specify the path /var/lib/etcd from the control
plane or machine template definitions.
• Define the variable under:
spec.topology.controlPlane.variables.overrides[kubernetes].value.etcdConfiguration.maximumDBSizeGiB
vSphere Kubernetes Service 3.5.0+v1.34
Release Snapshot
vSphere Kubernetes Service 3.5 is generally available for use with vSphere 9.x and vSphere 8.x.
Name Release Date
vSphere Kubernetes Service 3.5.0+v1.34 27 October 2025
What's New
• VKS Add-on Management- We've streamlined the management of VKS Standard Packages add-ons. This update
includes the following key improvements:
– Allowing an Addon Repository to be installed into all VKS clusters via AddonRepository/AddonRepositoryInstall
APIs. This will simplify the setup process for VKS Standard Packages, including when relocated to a private
registry. By default, an AddonRepository for VKS Standard Package embedded in the VKS Package will be used
(v2025.10.22 release for this VKS 3.5.0 release).
– Customers can register and update to another AddonRepository, for example, to use a version of the VKS Standard
Package different from what’s embedded in the VKS package, or when relocating the VKS Standard Package to a
private registry
– Allowing management of VKS Standard Packages via the Supervisor Namespace, including installation, upgrades,
and configurations. Users can consume this via VKS Cluster Management introduced in VCF 9.0.1 or the new VCF
CLI ‘addon’ plugin.
– As part of Cluster k8s version upgrades, VKS will perform add-on compatibility pre-checks and will upgrade add-ons
to ensure the clusters are using the latest compatible AddonReleases. If the compatibility pre-checks fail, VKS will
block the upgrades with suitable error messages.
– As part of installing/upgrading add-ons on the Cluster, VKS will run a set of pre-checks, including migration checks
to block duplicate PackageInstalls and dependency checks to report non-blocking errors for add-ons with missing
dependencies.
– Simplifying the installation of the Cluster Autoscaler add-on and allowing it to be automatically upgraded as a part of
Cluster upgrades.
VMware by Broadcom 44

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
– AddonReconciled condition on the Cluster resource will now aggregate the reconciled status of all VKS-managed
add-ons installed on the cluster, including any VKS Standard Packages add-ons. If the condition AddonReconciled
is not true, Cluster k8s version upgrade pre-checks will fail, blocking the Cluster upgrade.,
– Make it easier to discover new versions and associated compatibility metadata for AddonReleases
• Introducing Cluster API v1beta2: This release introduces v1beta2 versions for core Cluster API resources (e.g.,
Cluster, Machine) and their associated Bootstrap, and Control Plane objects. To ensure a smooth transition, any new
or existing clusters created with the previous v1beta1 API will be automatically converted to the v1beta2 API by
the upgraded Cluster API controllers. Going forward it is recommended to use v1beta2 API to manage the LCM of
Kubernetes cluster.
– v1beta2 API version marks an important step in the journey towards graduating our API to v1
– Status has been improved across all resources for easier troubleshooting
• PodDisruptionBudgets (PDBs) - A new condition SystemChecksSucceeded has been added to the Cluster
object. This condition indicates whether the cluster has passed existing all pre-update system checks related to
PodDisruptionBudgets (PDBs). If there is any PDB with 'allowedDisruptions <=0', this condition will be false. Cluster
K8s version upgrade will be blocked if this condition is false.
Note - Any PDB which has no matching Pods may indicate a misconfiguration, such as an erroneous selector. Such
PDBs will also have allowedDisruptions will be 0, and will therefore block upgrade.
• Customizing Kubernetes Configuration - The new builtin-generic-v3.5.0 ClusterClass provides fine-grained
configuration control over core Kubernetes components and OS security settings, enabling performance tuning and
compliance requirements:
– API Server Configuration (kubernetes.apiServerConfiguration) - Configure request handling with concurrent
request limits (maxRequestsInFlight, maxMutatingRequestsInFlight), structured logging (text or JSON format,
verbosity levels 0-6, flush frequency), request timeouts, and profiling controls for high-load environments.
– etcd Configuration (kubernetes.etcdConfiguration) - Set etcd database size limits with maximumDBSizeGiB (2-8
GiB range). The system automatically provisions 25% additional volume capacity and maps to etcd's --quota-
backend-bytes flag to prevent cluster outages from quota exhaustion. Starting with ClusterClass v3.5, ETCD
storage sizing is now managed exclusively through this variable-based configuration mechanism. Directly mounting
or providing a custom /var/lib/etcd volume is no longer supported (and was never a supported configuration path).
The platform now automatically provisions and manages the ETCD volume and quota based on the configured
variable value. Users should remove any manual bind-mounts or scripts targeting the ETCD data directory to
ensure compatibility and reliable cluster operation.
– kubelet Configuration (kubernetes.kubeletConfiguration) - Comprehensive node agent configuration including
pod limits (maxPods per node, 20-110), image management (pull behavior, GC thresholds, parallel pulls, credential
verification policies), structured logging, container log rotation, registry rate limiting (QPS controls), and unsafe
sysctls allowlist for specialized workloads. Can be overridden per control plane or worker pool.
– GRUB Password Protection (osConfiguration.grub.password) - Enable GRUB bootloader password protection
on Linux nodes with PBKDF2 SHA-512 hashed password (auto-generates if not provided) to prevent unauthorized
boot parameter modification. Required for CIS and STIG security benchmark compliance. Can be overridden per
control plane or worker pool.
– Sudo Password Requirements (osConfiguration.user.requirePasswordOnSudo) - Enforce password
authentication for sudo operations, implementing principle of least privilege by removing NOPASSWD directive from
sudoers configuration. Required for STIG security benchmark compliance. Can be overridden per control plane or
worker pool.
All new variables are optional and backward-compatible. To use these features, specify builtin-generic-v3.5.0 in your
cluster topology.
• VCF CLI Plugin changes:
– Change Cluster plugin to consume v1beta2 Cluster API
– Add a new 'addon' cli plugin to manage addons and migrate PackageInstalls to consume addons
– Adjust cluster status conditions in Cluster plugin according to v1beta2 Cluster API conditions
• Integrated Support Bundler within VCF CLI - VKS 3.5 now integrates the VKS Cluster Support Bundler directly into
the VCF CLI. This enhancement allows users to effortlessly collect all necessary support diagnostic information for
workload clusters via the support-bundle subcommand within the VCF CLI's cluster plugin, eliminating the need for a
separate tool download.

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1

– Skip Temporary User Creation: A new --skip-create-user flag allows users to bypass the creation of temporary
users during support bundler operations.
– Selective Log Collection: The tool can now selectively collect logs only from control plane nodes, rather than the
entire cluster.
– Network Logs: vks-support-bundler now includes network log collection, which will assist in diagnosing network-
related issues.

Note: This unscheduled rollout only affects the control plane nodes, and workloads running on the cluster should remain
unaffected
Workaround:
There is no workaround available for this issue, as it stems from an incorrect inference of the base version of the custom
CC (in this case, 3.4.0).
Adding a content library to the supervisor with a duplicate KR version template (matching the cluster's KR
version) can cause the VKS cluster to enter a false state.
The cluster status will report "False" for the TopologyReconciled condition, with the message: "error computing the desired
state of the Cluster topology: failed to apply patches: failed to generate patches for patch "default": failed to call extension
handler "generate-patches.runtime-extension": got failure response."
Note: This condition does not impact the runtime availability of existing nodes, so current workloads on the cluster will
continue to run. It only affects future reconciliation and updates.
Workaround:
1. Delete the conflicting OS template from the newly added content library.
OR
2. Update the cluster's "run.tanzu.vmware.com/resolve-os-image" annotation with the content library ID.
An error will occur if the /var/lib/etcd volume mount and maximumDBSizeGiB are defined during cluster creation
or updates..
Clusters that retain a manual /var/lib/etcd volume mount after upgrading to VKS 3.5.0 will continue operating in a legacy
configuration and will not benefit from the new automated ETCD volume provisioning and quota management introduced
with the maximumDBSizeGiB variable.
Workaround:
• Edit the Cluster object and remove any user-defined volume mounts that specify the path /var/lib/etcd from the control
plane or machine template definitions.
• Define the variable under:
spec.topology.controlPlane.variables.overrides[kubernetes].value.etcdConfiguration.maximumDBSizeGiB
Resolution:
Use maximumDBSizeGiB variable to configure etcd volume for clusters.

About the vSphere Kubernetes Service 3.4 Release Notes
vSphere Kubernetes Service (VKS) provides components for provisioning and managing the lifecycle of Kubernetes
clusters in the vSphere Supervisor environment.
These release notes provide details for each VKS release. Refer to the Managing vSphere Kubernetes Service with
vSphere Supervisor documentation for usage information.
Versioning and Upgrades
vSphere Kubernetes Service (VKS) 3.4.x point releases do not introduce a new or different ClusterClass. They deliver the
same base 3.4.0 ClusterClass, bundled with cumulative bug fixes and underlying improvements.
To ensure cluster stability and receive critical bug fixes, always upgrade to the latest available point release. For the core
requirements, refer back to the baseline VKS 3.4.0+v1.33.
Prerequisites for VKS 3.4 Upgrade
• vCenter and Supervisor Kubernetes version - VKS 3.4 requires Supervisor Kubernetes version 1.29 or later.
Supervisor Kubernetes version 1.29 is available with vCenter 9 or vCenter 8 Update 3b. You must upgrade the
Supervisor Kubernetes version in vCenter to at least version 1.29.
• VKr version - VKS 3.4 drops compatibility for VKr 1.28. Before upgrading the VKS version on the Supervisor to VKS
3.4, you must ensure all your VKS Clusters are running at least on VKr 1.29.
• VKS version - To upgrade to VKS 3.4 directly, the VKS version installed on the Supervisor must be at least VKS 3.1. If
you are using VKS 3.0, you need to upgrade to VKS 3.1 or later before upgrading to VKS 3.4.
Note:
VKS 3.2 introduced ClusterClass versioning, which affects upgrades from 3.1 to later versions. Refer to the
vSphere Kubernetes Service 3.2 section of these Release Notes for details before upgrading from 3.1 or earlier.
Deprecation Announcements
• With the release of VKS 3.4, we introduce and recommend using the builtin-generic-v3.4.0 ClusterClass. Existing
clusters will need to rebase to builtin-generic-v3.4.0 as a part of, or prior to, any upgrade to Kubernetes v1.33 or later
(For more information, see link) Additionally, the tanzukubernetescluster, builtin-generic-v3.1.0, builtin-generic-v3.2.0,
and builtin-generic-v3.3.0 ClusterClass are considered deprecated and will be removed in future releases.
• With the release of VKS 3.4, we recommend using builtin-generic-v3.4.0 as the foundation for any Custom
ClusterClass. Existing Custom ClusterClass should be rebased onto builtin-generic-v3.4.0. (For more information, see
link.) Custom ClusterClass based on the tanzukubernetescluster, builtin-generic-v3.1.0, builtin-generic-v3.2.0, and
builtin-generic-v3.3.0 ClusterClass are also considered deprecated.

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
Known Issues
Cluster lifecycle operations (creation, scaling, and updates) are blocked following a certificate rotation
When attempting to create or update a cluster, the TopologyReconciled condition reports a failure. Customers will see
error messages such as tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority specifically when
Cluster API attempts to call the runtime-extension-webhook-service.
Manually restart the Cluster API or runtime-extension pods to force a reload of the certificates from the mounted volumes.
Refer to https://knowledge.broadcom.com/external/article?articleNumber=424003
Fixed Issues
Creation and Upgrading workload clusters may sometimes fail
Steps to Reproduce
1. Upgrade the VKS service version to 3.4.0 or 3.4.1
2. Perform one of the three actions
– Create a new Cluster with CC versions builtin-generic-v3.2.0, builtin-generic-v3.3.0
– Upgrade the Kubernetes version of an existing Cluster using CC versions builtin-generic-v3.2.0 or builtin-generic-
v3.3.0
– Upgrade the Kubernetes version of an existing Cluster using CC version builtin-generic-v3.1.0 and removing the
kubernetes.vmware.com/skip-auto-cc-rebase annotation from the Cluster object
3. Cluster operation might fail with the error mentioned below. This scenario is more likely to be observed following a
VKS upgrade due to stale entries in the cache.
Error Details
k edit cluster <cluster-name> -n some-namespace error: clusters.cluster.x-k8s.io<cluster-
name> could not be patched: admission
webhookcapi.mutating.tanzukubernetescluster.run.tanzu.vmware.com" denied the request:
Cluster and variable validation failed: [spec.topology.variables[vmClass]: Invalid value:
"\"best-effort-small\"": variable is not defined, spec.topology.variables[storageClass]:
Invalid value: "\"vsansp\"": variable is not defined, spec.topology.variables[volumes]:
Invalid value: " [{\"capacity\":\"5Gi\",\"mountPath\":\"/var/lib/etcd\",
\"name\":\"etcd\",\"storageClass\":\"vsansp\"}]": variable is not defined,
spec.topology.variables[kubernetes]: Invalid value: "{\"certificateRotation\": {\"enabled
\":true,\"renewalDaysBeforeExpiry\":90}}"
Workaround:
Restart the deployment `vmware-system-tkg-webhook` in the service namespace (i.e svc-tkg-*) and retry the cluster
operation.
If the cluster was originally created in vCenter v7.x or vCenter 8.0 GA then upgrading from KR v1.32 to KR v1.33
or an upgrade using builtin-generic-v3.3.0 (or higher) clusterclass might fail.
Please see Steps to Perform Before Upgrading to ClusterClass 3.3.0 or KR 1.32.X to 1.33.X for more information and
workaround.
This issue is fixed in vSphere Kubernetes Service 3.4.2, and the workaround does not need to be applied if environments
are upgraded to VKS 3.4.2 prior to cluster upgrades.

VMware by Broadcom 49

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
What's New
Security updates and Bug fixes
Known Issues
If the cluster was originally created in vCenter v7.x or vCenter 8.0 GA then upgrading from KR v1.32 to KR v1.33
or an upgrade using builtin-generic-v3.3.0 (or higher) clusterclass might fail.
Please see Steps to Perform Before Upgrading to ClusterClass 3.3.0 or KR 1.32.X to 1.33.X for more information and
workaround.
This issue is fixed in vSphere Kubernetes Service 3.5.0, and the workaround does not need to be applied if environments
are upgraded to VKS 3.5.0 prior to cluster upgrades.
Fixed Issues
Extra VPC association is created
With VKS 3.4.0, an extra VPC association was created for the VKS managed vmware-system-vks-public namespace.
This was not necessary and was reducing the number of VPCs available for use by 1. This issue has been addressed and
no new VPC association is created for this namespace.
Ensure Only FIPS validated KEX in sshd config
STIG compliance scanning may report non-approved FIPS Key Exchange Algorithm are used when FIPS mode is
enabled for Guest Clusters. This issue has been addressed in this release.
Validate Cluster's Pod/Service CIDR only during Cluster creation
In order to support existing clusters with incorrect CIDR values, the new validations will only be applied on during Cluster
creation.
Kubernetes Release (KR) deletion is stuck if corresponding Tanzu Kubernetes release (TKr) is not found
This issue is addressed in this release.
Mark storage class in CC volume variable as optional
The StorageClass field in the volumes variable across all ClusterClass versions greater than 3.2.0 was marked as
mandatory in the earlier VKS versions. This change has been reverted in this version, which allows Cluster operations
with the volume variables to not mandate setting the field in the variable. When left unset, the default storage class from
the vSphere Namespace is used for volume creation.
vSphere Kubernetes Service 3.4.0+v1.33
Release Snapshot
vSphere Kubernetes Service 3.4 is generally available for use with vSphere 9.0 and vSphere 8.x.
Name Release Date
vSphere Kubernetes Service 3.4 17 JUN 2025
What's New
• Lifecycle and Upgrades
– Support for Kubernetes minor version 1.33 - This release of VKS 3.4 adds compatibility for Kubernetes release
version 1.33. To upgrade your VKS clusters to v1.33, you must upgrade the VKS version running on the Supervisor
to VKS 3.4. Refer to the Product Lifecycle page for the updated Support period of VKr.
VMware by Broadcom 50

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
– Extended Support for Kubernetes - To enable stable environment for business-critical applications for longer
periods of time, we are announcing Extended Support for certain VKr versions. VKr 1.33 is the first VKr release that
comes with Extended Support.
– Specify Ubuntu OS Version - VKr 1.33 supports Ubuntu 24.04 along with Ubuntu 22.04. To resolve either Ubuntu
22.04 or Ubuntu 24.04, Cluster object definitions with Ubuntu nodes will require an explicit field for and
os-name
in the ClusterClass topology annotations. Whether you are creating a new v 1.33 cluster, or upgrading
os-version
from v1.32 to v1.33, you must update the annotation in the cluster object configuration to
resolve-os-image
reflect the Ubuntu version number.
For example:
run.tanzu.vmware.com/resolve-os-image: "os-name=ubuntu,os-version=24.04"
• Support for Istio Service Mesh Standard Package - VKS 3.4 introduces support for Standard Package, Istio,
enabling the platform engineers to leverage Service mesh capabilities. Beyond standard installation and upgrade
support, Broadcom will provide additional support in the investigation and analysis of any Istio related incidents in your
VKS environment.
• Cluster API Improvements and Updates
– New builtin-generic-v3.4.0 ClusterClass.
– Efficient ClusterClass consumption across namespaces.
• VKS 3.4 introduces a more efficient way of sharing and referencing ClusterClass. Each ClusterClass shipped
with VKS is now centrally hosted in the namespace, from where the
vmware-system-vks-public
ClusterClass definition can be referenced, instead of replicating it in each namespace. This change will not
require any modifications to the existing clusters.
• Custom ClusterClass present in a namespace can now be optionally shared across namespaces.
• ClusterClass builtin-generic-v3.3.0 and below will remain available in all namespaces to retain backwards
compatibility.
• Customizable StorageClass Labels and Annotations - VKS version 3.4 provides the ability to define custom labels
and annotations for StorageClass instances that are synced from the Supervisor to the VKS cluster. This functionality
guarantees that StorageClass metadata within the VKS cluster can be configured for use by various components,
including external backup tools.
• Validations during creation and modification of v1beta1 Clusters - Improving on the existing validations, this
release adds safe guards when creating or modifying v1beta1 clusters. A range of new validations have been
implemented to prevent potential failures. Validations include: proxy configuration, user-supplied trusted certificates,
preventing ClusterClass downgrades, StorageClass reference integrity, ensuring namespace-attached VMclasses
are the only ones used in ClusterClass, service domain conformance to RFC 1123, minimum ClusterClass checks for
Windows nodepools, and nodepool uniqueness, among others.
• Blocking the use of TanzuKubernetesCluster API creation of new VKS clusters - Cluster API is now the default
method for bootstrapping, configuring, and managing Kubernetes clusters, replacing TanzuKubernetesCluster API.
However, starting version 3.4, you won’t be able to use the deprecated TKC API to create Kubernetes 1.33 cluster,
or upgrade an existing cluster to Kubernetes release 1.33. You will still be able to create a Kubernetes release 1.32
cluster or lower with the TKC API.
Note:
When using Consumption Interface v1.0.2, creating a TKC cluster with default configuration will fail as that
defaults to VKr 1.33. You must use the Cluster v1beta1 API for creating clusters starting with VKr 1.33.
Note:
The deprecation of the TKC API is announced in VKS 3.2 (see link). The VKS 3.3 provides support for a
streamlined method to retire the TKC resources for existing clusters. (see blog).
• Others
– Automatic password rotation before expiration - To avoid lock-outs due to password expiration for vmware-
system-user, VKS 3.4 features rotating passwords automatically before their expiration. Making it seamless, yet
secure for platform engineers to connect to the VKS clusters using SSH, while adhering to established security
hardening protocols.

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
– Improvements to Support Bundler - VKS 3.4 introduces a number of improvements to the Support Bundler
including additional support data like etcd metrics and a number of bug fixes. You can read more about the Support
Bundler here.
– Updated VKS Versioning - From VKS 3.4 onwards, a new versioning system is available. The versioning will be of
the format x.y.z+v1.nn ( - VKS version, is the Kubernetes minor version this release adds support for),
x.y.z 1.nn
for example:
• 3.4.0+v1.33 (for version 3.4.0, adding support to 1.33, interoperability with 1.33, 1.32, 1.31, 1.30, 1.29)
• 3.4.1-embedded+v1.33 (when VKS is embedded in Supervisor).

No Upgrade Path for VKr 1.28.15 Clusters When Upgrading from VKS 3.1.1 to VKS 3.4.0
On vSphere 8.0.3 P04 with embedded VKS 3.1.1, clusters running VKr 1.28.15 cannot be upgraded directly to VKS 3.4.0.
The upgrade fails during the precheck because VKS 3.4.0 no longer supports VKr 1.28.15. However, VKr 1.29.15 is not
compatible with VKS 3.1.1, which prevents an intermediate upgrade.
VMware by Broadcom 52

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
Workaround:
To perform a successful upgrade to VKS 3.4.0, follow these steps:
1. Upgrade from VKS 3.1.1 to VKS 3.3.3.
2. Upgrade the VKr 1.28.15 clusters to VKr 1.29.15.
3. Upgrade to VKS 3.4.0.
Ubuntu Pro and FIPS Not Enabled on Version 1.33.1 Ubuntu Clusters Without os-name Annotation
On VKS 3.4.0, Ubuntu Pro and FIPS are not enabled on Ubuntu 1.33.1 clusters if the annotation is missing.
os-name
Ubuntu cluster creation succeeds when only the annotation is provided, but the enablement of Ubuntu Pro
os-version
and FIPS does not occur as expected. No error is reported during cluster provisioning.
Workaround:
To enable Ubuntu Pro and FIPS:
• For existing clusters, add the annotation to the cluster configuration.
os-name
• For new clusters, include both and annotations during deployment.
os-name os-version
Fixed Issues
• Cluster object reports Available as false after upgrade to v1beta2 conditions
This issue has been fixed in VKS 3.4.0.
• Update of several Cluster variables or the Harbor Supervisor Service cert on an existing VKS cluster does not
trigger an automatic rolling update of VKS cluster nodes
Issue exists in VKS 3.3.0–3.3.2 and is fixed in VKS 3.3.3 and VKS 3.4.0.
• Additional TrustedCAs configured for a TanzuKubernetesCluster are lost when the TanzuKubernetesCluster is
retired and replaced with a Cluster resource
Workloads might fail with TLS errors, and bootstrap might fail due to missing trusted CA secrets.
Issue exists in VKS 3.3.0–3.3.2 and is fixed in VKS 3.3.3 and VKS 3.4.0.
• Containerd is not restarted after CA certificates are installed, which prevents it from trusting the new
certificates
Issue exists in VKS 3.3.0–3.3.2 and is fixed in VKS 3.3.3 and VKS 3.4.0.
• Kubernetes LoadBalancer services created with TanzuKubernetesCluster might be disrupted after
TanzuKubernetesCluster is retired if it was upgraded from a legacy to a non-legacy Kubernetes release
In NSX environments with routable pods, related Supervisor resources are also deleted after TKC retirement. These
are now re-parented to the Cluster.
Issue exists in VKS 3.3.0–3.3.2 and is fixed in VKS 3.3.3 and VKS 3.4.0.

Name Release Date

What's New
• Support for VKr 1.32. This release adds support for VKr version 1.32 and drops the compatibility for VKr 1.27.x. This
release also drops compatibility for 1.31.1 and adds support for 1.31.4. To upgrade to vSphere Kubernetes Service
3.3.0, all vSphere Kubernetes Service (VKS) clusters must be running VKr 1.28 or higher.. Refer to the interoperability
matrix for more details.
• Ability to enable OS FIPS mode - This release provides a configuration option to enable Operating System FIPS on
the vSphere Kubernetes Service cluster nodes during the creation of the VKS clusters. Refer to the documentation
to make these configuration changes for different operating systems (Photon OS, Ubuntu, Windows). Ubuntu Pro
subscription is required when using a Ubuntu based vSphere Kubernetes Service cluster.
• Ability to configure a Windows node pool to use Group Managed Service Accounts - This release supports
the joining of Windows nodes to on-premises Active Directory infrastructure to make use of Group Managed Service
Accounts. The service automates the joining of Windows nodes to an Active Directory domain within a particular
organizational unit, and adding nodes to a security group that can be delegated to for access to group managed
service accounts.
• Support for migration from TKC API to Cluster API - Deprecation of TanzuKubernetesCluster API was announced
in vSphere Kubernetes Service release 3.2. The API will be removed no sooner than June 2025. Customers are
encouraged to use the cluster-api to bootstrap, configure and manage the lifecycle of the Kubernetes clusters. This
release provides a means to retire the TKC API and continue managing existing VKS clusters using the cluster-api’s
Cluster API.
• Cluster Autoscaler supports scaling from zero or to zero - This release removes the no scaling from zero or to
zero limitation for autoscaler for clusters running VKr 1.31.4 or higher. You need to have the autoscaler standard
package installed. Please refer to the documentation for more details.

Please see Steps to Perform Before Upgrading to ClusterClass 3.3.0 or VKr 1.32.X to 1.33.X for more information and
workaround. This issue is fixed in vSphere Kubernetes Service 3.5.0, and the workaround does not need to be applied if
environments are upgraded to VKS 3.5.0 prior to cluster upgrades.
See KB410481
After a retiring VKS cluster, Scale up or upgrade operation on the cluster area stuck with VMs in pending state
When configured on VKS cluster, additional Trusted CA, creates a secret with the base64-encoded certificate data. This
secret is deleted when the VKS cluster is retired and its ownership is not transferred to the cluster object. Thus, any scale
up or upgrade operation on the cluster fails due to the missing secret. If the VKS cluster has already been retired and was
configured with Additional Trusted CA, following error will be seen in the new machine being provisioned:
*Relevant log’s location*: Bootstrap ready condition for the machine will be in false
state with a similar error. - lastTransitionTime: "2025-03-28T00:09:48Z" message:
'failed to resolve file source: secret not found: <NAMESPACE>/<CLUSTER_NAME>-user-trusted-
ca-secret: secrets "<CLUSTER_NAME>-user-trusted-ca-secret" not found' reason:
DataSecretGenerationFailed severity: Warning status: "False" type: BootstrapReady
Refer to Retiring a TanzuKubernetesCluster (TKC) with Additional Trusted CA Certificates for workaround and preventive
action before retiring TKC if it uses Additional Trusted CA.
Cluster object reports as false after upgrade to v1beta2 conditions
Available
VKS 3.3 includes CAPI v1.9.3, which introduces v1beta2 conditions in the Cluster status. After an upgrade to
a version with v1beta2 conditions, the and conditions
DataSecretAvailable CertificatesAvailable
in objects are missing. This is due to an upstream bug #11948. This issue affects the cluster’s overall
kubeadmconfig
v1beta2 condition.
Available
Workaround: None. This issue will be resolved in an upcoming VKS release with CAPI 1.10+.
Updates to several specific cluster variables and Harbor Supervisor Service certificates do not trigger automatic
rolling update of the nodes
Changes to several specific cluster variables or Harbor Supervisor Service certificates on an existing cluster do not trigger
an automatic rolling update. As a result, configuration changes will not propagate to the nodes.
Workaround: For more details and a workaround, see the Broadcom KB article 391589.
DaemonSet pods are stuck in "Pending" state on autoscaler based classy clusters
The autoscaler is scaling nodes one at a time and the order in which all pods are scheduled is random. If other types of
pods are scheduled before the DeamonSet type pods, the DeamonSet pods might not be scheduled if node's resource is
exhausted. At this time, even if the pods are in the pending state, the autoscaler will not automatically scale new worker
nodes and shows
cluster-autoscaler pod didn't trigger scale-up: 1 node(s) didn't match Pod's
. Because the DeamonSet pod is always adding an affinity to each pod and locks it to the
node affinity/selector
current node, the autoscaler believes that scaling a new node cannot accommodate these pending pods because the new
node does not meet the node affinity, so the pods remain in the pending state.
Workaround: Set a priority class specific for DaemonSets with a relatively high value to ensure they are scheduled ahead
of most of other pods.
Do not delete the pending pods manually, because they have node affinity and will be scheduled to the original nodes
again.
Antrea pod is stuck in pending state after a Windows Cluster upgrade from 1.31.4 to 1.32.0

When attempting to create a hybrid cluster with workers consisting of Photon, Windows, and Ubuntu using the Cloud

vSphere Kubernetes Service 3.0
Release Snapshot
vSphere Kubernetes Service 3.0 is generally available for use with vSphere 8 Update 3.
Name Release Date
vSphere Kubernetes Service 3.0 25 JUN 2024
What's New
Prior to vSphere 8.0 Update 3, vSphere Kubernetes Service (VKS) components responsible for the lifecycle of VKS
clusters were delivered as part of vCenter releases. Starting with the vSphere 8.0 Update 3 release, VKS components
are decoupled from vCenter and packaged as a Supervisor service which can be updated and managed independent of
vCenter releases.
With this flexibility, VKS releases are delivered two ways: independent and bundled with vCenter. When released
independently, you can register and upgrade the VKS separate from upgrading vCenter. When bundled with vCenter, after
upgrading vCenter the VKS is automatically registered for upgrade. Refer to the Managing vSphere Kubernetes Service
and Workloads documentation for details.
VKS 3.0 is the first release of the decoupled VKS. It is available as part of the vSphere 8.0 Update 3 release. The system
automatically installs VKS 3.0 when you install or upgrade to the vSphere Supervisor component versions listed in the
table. Once installed, you can upgrade to subsequent VKS releases, such as VKS 3.1, 3.2, and so on.
Component Required Version
vCenter Server 8.0 Update 3 (8.0.3)
vSphere Namespaces 0.1.9
Supervisor 1.28.3, 1.27.5, 1.26.8
VKr v1.25.7 or later for vSphere 8.x
Known Issues
VKS 3.0 has the following known issues.
One of the OSImages might be missing from non-legacy VKr >= v1.28 if vSphere is upgraded from 7.x to 8.x.
Description: If, after upgrading from vSphere 7.x to 8.x, you list available VKrs for vSphere 8.x, you may not see both
OSImages. For example, the following command returns only one OSImage when you should see two (must be run from
the vSphere Namespace where a VKS cluster is provisioned):
kubectl get osimage -A | grep 1.28
Workaround: Delete any non-legacy VKr >=v1.28 and wait for it to be re-created which will happen after approximately
10 minutes. The recreated VKr will have both the Photon and Ubuntu images, and the OSImage Kuberentes resources
will also be created for both Photon and Ubuntu.
If you cannot wait for the VKr to be recreated, you can delete the active
vmware-system-tkg-controller-manager
pod which will recreate the VKr.
Supervisor backup taken via TMC with VKS 3.0 installed does not restore after 8 hours due to token expiration.
Description: On a TMC-managed cluster, after restoring a Supervisor from backup taken with VKS 3.0, the TMC agent is
in a CrashLoopBackoff state.
Workaround: Reregister the cluster with TMC.

Introduction
VMware vSphere Kubernetes releases | 18 June 2026
Check for additions and updates to these release notes.
vSphere Kubernetes releases
VMware vSphere Kubernetes releases (VKrs) provide you with Kubernetes software distributions signed and supported
by VMware for provisioning vSphere Kubernetes Service (VKS) clusters in the vSphere Supervisor environment. VMware
VKrs follow the upstream Kubernetes versioning.
This document contains release notes for VKrs 1.25.x and later. For earlier VKr versions, see VMware VKr Release Notes
- VKr 1.24.x and Earlier.
Content Library
The availability of VKrs depends on the vCenter content library and its synchronization frequency. Use the command
to list the VKr that are available in your environment. If a release is not synchronized with your library,
kubectl get kr
that release will not appear in the list returned by the command. Refer to the Managing vSphere Kubernetes Service with
vSphere Supervisor documentation for more information.
About vSphere Kubernetes releases
Historically, vSphere Kubernetes releases (VKr), formerly known as Tanzu Kubernetes releases (TKrs) have been
distributed in two distinct formats: legacy and non-legacy. Each format was designed for compatibility with specific
vSphere versions and was clearly labeled to communicate its intended environment and upgrade path.
TKr Format Types ( see documentation )
• Legacy TKrs:
– Utilized an older format compatible with vSphere 7.x.
– Also supported on vSphere 8.x, but strictly for upgrade purposes.
– Identified by the legacy-tkr annotation label.
– Labeled as “for vSphere 7.x” in release notes and documentation.
• Non-Legacy TKrs:
– Introduced with vSphere 8.x, these TKrs support new features and enhanced compatibility.
– Exclusively compatible with vSphere 8.x.
– Labeled as “for vSphere 8.x” in release notes and documentation.
Previous Release Designations
Until recently, TKr releases included explicit version designations in their naming conventions and documentation, such
as:
• TKr v1.28.8 for vSphere 8.x (non-legacy)
• TKr v1.28.7 for vSphere 7.x (legacy)
This approach provided clear guidance on which TKr should be used for a given vSphere version and ensured smooth
upgrade paths.
Change in Versioning and Compatibility (Effective VKr 1.29)
Effective with VKr 1.29, the explicit “for vSphere m.n” designation will be discontinued, since the legacy TKrs are no longer
supported. A single VKr release (non-legacy) will now operate across both vSphere 8.x and 9.x platforms.
VMware by Broadcom 67

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
Compatibility and Upgrades
The VKrs for vSphere 8.x are updated to a package-based framework. While you can run vSphere 7.x VKrs on vSphere
8.x, you cannot take advantage of vSphere 8.x features unless you upgrade the cluster to use a VKr for vSphere 8.x.
Use the command to verify compatibility of VKrs with the vSphere Kubernetes Service. See also the
kubectl get kr
Compatibility Matrix section. Upgrading VKS clusters to a VKr for vSphere 8.x is allowed starting with the vSphere 8.0a
release. You must update existing VKS clusters to a minimum VKr v1.21.x or later before upgrading your environment
to vSphere 8.0a. After you have upgraded to vSphere 8.0a, update clusters to a VKr for vSphere 8.x format to take
advantage of new features. See the Updating vSphere Supervisor documentation for details.
Important:
Upgrading is only supported when the origin and target VKrs are the same operating system. For example, you
cannot upgrade from a Photon OS VKr to an Ubuntu VKr.
Components and Packages
Use the command to list components and packages. The VKr format that
kubectl get kr VKR_NAME -o yaml
supports provisioning VKS clusters on vSphere 8.x uses a package-based framework to deliver VMware software and
Kubernetes components.
STIG Hardening
VMware provides Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIG) for each vSphere Kubernetes release. See STIG
Hardening for details.
CRITICAL REQUIREMENT for vSphere 8.0.0 Customers
If you have deployed vSphere Supervisor 8.0.0 GA, be aware of the following CRITICAL REQUIRMENT.
Before upgrading to vSphere 8 U1 you must create a temporary VKr content library to avoid a known issue that causes
VKS Controller pods to go into CrashLoopBackoff when VKrs are pushed to the existing content library. To avoid this
issue, complete the following steps.
NOTE: This requirement does not apply to content libraries you use for VMs provisioned through VM Service.
1. Create a new subscribed content library with a temporary subscription URL pointing to https://wp-content.vmware.com/
v2/8.0.0/lib.json.
2. Synchronize all the items in the temporary content library.
3. Associate the temporary content library with the VKS.
4. Run the command and verify that all the VKrs are created.
kubectl get tkr
5. At this point the VKS Controller should be in a running state, which you can verify by listing the pods in the vSphere
Namespace.
6. If the VKS Controller is in CrashLoopBackOff (CLBO) state, restart the VKS Controller deployment using the following
command:
kubectl rollout restart deployment -n vmware-system-tkg vmware-system-tkg-controller-manager
7. Upgrade to vSphere 8 U1.
8. Update the VKS configuration to use the original subscribed content library at https://wp-content.vmware.com/v2/
latest/lib.json. NOTE: The content library is not namespace-scoped, so when you update one VKS configuration, the
change should be propagated to all others. You should verify this by checking each vSphere Namespace.

Packages are in 'Reconcile failed' state after upgrade due to caBundle certificate mismatch
After the cluster upgrades to this version, you may sometimes see that the packages are in 'Reconcile Failed' state. Due
to this the upgrade is flagged as failed. This may happen because the kapp-controller from the old cluster still exists
due to a possible race condition during the upgrade. Both the old and the new kapp-controller attempt to update the api
service with their CA bundle causing this issue.
Solution:
This issue has been addressed in this release.

After worker node scale-up and scale-down operation on large VKS cluster with 3CP/150W, with auto-scaler

This is caused due to a race condition in a scenario where auto-scaler is increasing the number of nodes, while there are
a larger number of pods waiting to be scheduled. And scheduler assigns the pods to the first few nodes available.

You can use the to clean up the failed jobs.

chrony finishes correcting the time, the kubelet will generate service tokens with past timestamps, rendering them
invalid.

After upgrade, application pods will be stuck in ContainerCreating state with warning
FailedAttachVolume
If a pod is stuck in state, execute the following command -

kubectl get pods -A | grep ContainerCreating"
Describe the pod, and if you find the following warning pattern, execute the workaround
2m9s (x59 over 104m) attachdetach-controller AttachVolume.Attach failed for volume
Warning FailedAttachVolume
"pvc-1f46ebd4-2606-4800-aa70-af8bdb75fdb8" : CSINode vks361-ph-336-calico-11ns5-c5-np1-worker-rf5zx-ttrqp-6qc7j
does not contain driver csi.vsphere.vmware.com
Workaround:
restart the csi-node pods
kubectl delete pod vsphere-csi-node-<xyz> -n vmware-system-csi
After worker node scale-up and scale-down operation on large VKS cluster with 3CP/150W, with auto-scaler
enabled, many pods can go into OutOfPods/Pending state.
This is caused due to a race condition in a scenario where auto-scaler is increasing the number of nodes, while there are
a larger number of pods waiting to be scheduled. And scheduler assigns the pods to the first few nodes available.
Workaround:
Delete the pods marked with the error "OutOfPods".
Autoscaler is unable to scale up windows nodes in a cluster containing multiple node pools with mixed OS types.
In autoscaler-based guest clusters having hybrid node pools with different OS (Photon, Ubuntu, Windows), when scaling
up applications on the clusters, Windows nodes are not scaled up even though Windows pods are in a pending state.
Workloads are stuck in a pending state and new nodes will not be deployed. The autoscaler pod logs show the error
can't schedule pod : predicate "NodeAffinity" didn't pass (predicateReasons=[node(s)
didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector];
Workaround:
When the cluster contains multiple node pools, the autoscaler will try to automatically scale up the node to handle pending
pods. When the pod contains nodeSelector, the autoscaler will simulate the node to be created based on the annotation
of the current node pool to evaluate whether it meets the needs of the current pod. Windows pods need nodeSelector to
schedule to Windows nodes, so this problem will be encountered.
Add the annotation(capacity.cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/labels: "key1=value1,key2=value2") in machine deployment
for windows to inform the autoscaler that this node pool can create nodes with this label.
After VKS cluster upgrade a failed Antrea upgrade job remains in the cluster
Sometimes, when the upgrades take longer you will notice an Antrea upgrade jobs in error state. These errors do not
impact the functionality of the Antrea. These are transient errors that occur while the cluster is upgrading.
Workaround:
You can use the to clean up the failed jobs.
kubectl delete

2.2 to 2.3.

generic-v3.7.0” /usr

for the removal of ExternalIPs in Kubernetes Services due to historical security concerns and better cloud-native
alternatives like LoadBalancers or Gateway APIs

Fixed Issues
VKS Clusters fail to deploy with error "rpc not supported for learner"
When a new control plane node joins an etcd cluster, it first enters a "learner" state where it syncs data but cannot vote.
At times, control plane node may become stuck in the “Provisioning” phase, preventing the cluster from completing. The
node successfully registers with etcd as a "learner" (a read-only replica) but is never promoted to a full voting member,
leaving the cluster unable to progress without manual intervention.
This issue has been fixed in VKr 1.35.5
Refer KB Article 439838
Ubuntu 24.04 Nodes unexpectedly transition to the NotReady state caused by a kernel panic
Workloads that trigger a specific kernel path are known to cause Ubuntu 24.04 nodes to unexpectedly transition to the
NotReady state triggering the restart of all residing Pods and consequently causing application outages on the affected
Node. VKr 1.35.5 upgraded the kernel version to address this issue.
