Working with VM Classes in vSphere Supervisor
To be able to self-service VMs in a Supervisor, DevOps users must have access to VM classes. A VM class is a template
that defines CPU, memory, and reservations for VMs. The VM class helps to set guardrails for the policy and governance
of VMs by anticipating development needs and accounting for resource availability and constraints.
The platform offers several default VM classes. A vSphere administrator can use them as is or create custom VM classes.
To make the classes available to the DevOps users, the vSphere administrator adds them to a namespace. The VM
classes assigned to the namespace can be used by stand-alone VMs and by the VMs that make up VKS clusters.
Automating VM Class Management
You can use the vSphere Client or the Data Center CLI (DCLI) to manually create and edit VM classes. To automate and
simplify these workflows, use the VMware PowerShell utilities for VKS.
The script supports the following management functions:
• Discover: Scans active VM configurations and generates a JSON file for conversion into VM classes.
• List: Displays all existing VM classes configured on a target vCenter instance.
• Backup: Exports and saves all VM classes from a vCenter to a JSON file.
• Update: Applies new or modified VM classes to a vCenter by using a JSON file generated automatically or created
manually.
• Delete: Removes specified VM classes from a vCenter.
To download the script and view detailed implementation guidelines, see the powershell-vks-utilities repository on GitHub.
Create a Custom VM Class Using the vSphere Client
As a vSphere administrator, you can use available default classes. You can also create custom VM classes instead of the
default and use them for VM deployment in a namespace.
Required privileges:
• Namespaces > Modify cluster-wide configuration
• Namespaces > Modify namespace configuration
• Virtual Machine Classes > Manage Virtual Machine Classes
When you create new classes, keep in mind the following considerations.
• VM classes that you create in a vCenter instance are available to all vCenter clusters and all namespaces in these
clusters.
• VM classes are available to all namespaces in vCenter. However, DevOps engineers can use only those VM classes
that you associate with a particular namespace.
Note:
You can also create VM classes using the DCLI command. See Create and Manage VM Classes Using the Data
Center CLI.
1. Go to the VM Service page.
a) From the vSphere Client home menu, select Supervisor Management.
b) Click the Services tab and click Manage on the VM Service pane.
2. On the VM Service page, click VM Classes and click Create VM Class.
3. On the Name page, specify the VM class name and click Next.
The VM class name Identifies the VM class. Enter a unique DNS compliant name that follows these requirements:
• Use a unique name that does not duplicate the names of default or custom VM classes in your environment.
• Use alphanumeric string with maximum length of 63 characters.
• Do not use uppercase letters or spaces.
• Use a dash anywhere except as a first or last character. For example, .
vm-class1
VMware by Broadcom 373

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
After you create the VM class, you cannot change its name.
4. On the Compatibility page, select the VM class hardware compatibility and click Next.
For more information, see Virtual Machine Compatibility in the vSphere documentation.
Note:
You can only set the hardware compability of a VM class during its creaiton and you cannot change it later.
5. On the Configuration page, leave the defaults.
6. On the Review and Confirm page, review the details and click Finish.
Edit the VM class configuration such as VM hardware and VM options.
Edit a VM Class Using the vSphere Client
Checkout how to edit a VM class after its creation. You can configure hardware resources such as CPU, memory, and
devices as well as edit VM options and advanced parameters. You can also edit default VM classes that Supervisors offer.
Required privileges:
• Namespaces > Modify cluster-wide configuration
• Namespaces > Modify namespace configuration
• Virtual Machine Classes > Manage Virtual Machine Classes
Editing a VM class does not result in automatic reconfiguring of the VMs that were previously deployed from this class.
For example, if a DevOps user created a VKS cluster with the VM class and you later change the VM class definition,
existing VKS VMs remain unaffected. New VKS VMs will use the modified class definition.
CAUTION:
If you scale out a VKS cluster after editing a VM class used by that cluster, new cluster nodes use the updated
class definition, but existing cluster nodes continue to use the initial class definition, resulting in a mismatch. Both
control plane and worker nodes can be scaled. For information about scaling, see Scale a Workload Cluster in the
vSphere Supervisor Services and Standalone Components documentation.
When you delete a VM class, it is removed from all associated namespaces. DevOps users can no longer self-service
VMs using this VM class. VMs that have already been created with this VM class are not affected.
1. In the vSphere Client, display available VM classes.
a) From the vSphere Client home menu, select Supervisor Management.
b) Click the Services tab and click the VM Service pane.
c) On the VM Service page, click VM Classes.
All default or user-created VM classes appear under Available VM Classes.
2. In the selected VM class pane, click Manage and click Edit.
3. In the Virtual Hardware page, configure the hardware resources of the VM class, such as memory, CPU, and different
devices.
All the VM hardware settings are applied when a DevOps user assigns the VM class to a VM. For example, the CPU
configuration values become the CPU resources dedicated to all the VMs that DevOps user creates by using the VM
class.
Note:
Starting from vSphere 8.0 Update 2b, the wizard for creating and editing VM classes changes from setting CPU
and memory resources in percentages to numeric values in MB, GB, TB, and HMz. For all previously created VM

VM Configuration Option Description
RDM Disk Add a raw device mapping (RDM) to store virtual machine data directly on a SAN LUN,

Host USB Device Add one or more USB passthrough devices from an ESXi host to a virtual machine if the

NVDIMM Configure a virtual NVDIMM device to the VM class to enable it to use non-volatile, or

SCSI Controller Controller Conditions, Limitations, and Compatibility in vSphere Virtual Machine

Administration.

your Supervisor environment have one or more NVIDIA GRID GPU graphics devices. You
can also configure other PCI devices on an ESXi host to make them available to a VM in a
passthrough mode.
If you select this option, the memory resource reservation value automatically changes to
100%.
For more information and additional requirements, see Deploying a VM with PCI Devices in
Supervisor Environment.

performance within a virtual machine. See How do I Add a Virtual Watchdog Timer Device to
a Virtual Machine in vSphere Virtual Machine Administration.

VM Configuration Option Description

provides a virtual machine with access to the system time of the primary ESXi host. See
How do I Add a Precision Clock Device to a Virtual Machine in vSphere Virtual Machine
Administration.
Serial Port Configure a connection of the virtual serial port to a physical serial port or to a file on the
host computer. See Change the Serial Port Configuration in vSphere Virtual Machine

Instance Storage Configure instance storage to the VM. Along with persistent storage volumes, a VM can
use instance storage. Unlike persistent volumes that exist separately from the VM, instance

Using the Instance Storage option, you can add appropriate storage policies and configure
volumes to be used with the VM.
For additional requirements, see Deploy a VM with Instance Storage in vSphere Supervisor.

must be configured to the vSphere Namespace where the VM runs. For more information

Associate a VM Class with a Namespace Using the vSphere Client
As a vSphere administrator, add a default or custom VM class to one or more namespaces on a Supervisor. When you
add a VM class to a namespace, you make the class available to DevOps users, so that they can start self-servicing VMs
in the Kubernetes namespace environment. The VM classes you assign to the namespace are also used by the VMs that
make up VKS clusters.
Required privileges:
• Namespaces > Modify cluster-wide configuration
• Namespaces > Modify namespace configuration
• Virtual Machine Classes > Manage Virtual Machine Classes
You can add multiple VM classes to a single namespace. Different VM classes serve as indicators of different levels
of service. If you publish multiple VM classes, DevOps users can select between all custom and default classes when
creating and managing virtual machines in the namespace.
Note:
To be able to deploy a VKS cluster in a newly created namespace, DevOps engineers need to have access to
VM classes. As a vSphere administrator, you must explicitly associate default or custom VM classes to any new
namespace where the VKS cluster is deployed.
VMware by Broadcom 376

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
1. In the vSphere Client, go to the namespace.
a) From the vSphere Client home menu, select Supervisor Management.
b) Click the Namespaces tab and click the namespace.
2. Add a VM class.
a) On the VM Service pane, click Add VM Class.
b) Select one or several VM classes and click OK.
The VM classes you added become available in the namespace for the DevOps to self-service VMs. These classes can
also be used by the VMs that make up VKS clusters.
Manage VM Classes on a Namespace Using the vSphere Client
After you associate a VM class with a namespace, you can add more VM classes or remove the class to unpublish it from
the Kubernetes namespace.
• If you want to remove a VM class from a namespace, verify that it is not used by VKS. Removing it can affect
operations VKS.
• Required privileges:
– Namespaces > Modify cluster-wide configuration
– Namespaces > Modify namespace configuration
– Virtual Machine Classes > Manage Virtual Machine Classes
1. In the vSphere Client, go to the namespace.
a) From the vSphere Client home menu, select Supervisor Management.
b) Click the Namespaces tab and click the namespace.
2. Add or remove a VM class.
a) On the VM Service pane, click Manage VM Class.
b) Perform one of the following operations.
Remove a VM class Deselect the VM class and click OK.
Add a VM class Select one or several VM classes and click OK.
Create and Manage VM Classes Using the Data Center CLI
In addition thevSphere Client, you can use the Data Center CLI (DCLI) commands to create and manage the VM classes.
The DCLI commands give you more flexibility and access to VM configuration options not available in thevSphere Client.
Prerequisites
Log in tovCenter using the root user account and type to use the DCLI in interactive mode.
dcli +i
For information about DCLI commands, see Overview of Running DCLI Commands.
Available DCLI Commands
Command Description
namespacemanagement virtualmachineclasses create Create a VM class object.
namespacemanagement virtualmachineclasses delete Delete the VM class object.
namespacemanagement virtualmachineclasses get Return information about a VM class.
namespacemanagement virtualmachineclasses list Return information about all VM classes.
namespacemanagement virtualmachineclasses update Update configuration of the VM class object.
VMware by Broadcom 377

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
Create a VM Class Using Data Center CLI
As a vSphere administrator, use the DCLI
com vmware vcenter namespacemanagement virtualmachineclasses
command to create a VM class. You can configure such VM properties as CPU, memory, memory reservations,
create
network adapters, and so on.
The command takes the following arguments.
Argument Description
-h, --help Show this help message and exit.
--config-spec CONFIG_SPEC A VirtualMachineConfigSpec associated with the VM class (json
input).
--cpu-count CPU_COUNT Required. The number of CPUs configured for virtual machine of
this class (integer).
--cpu-reservation CPU_RESERVATION The percentage of total available CPUs reserved for a virtual
machine (integer).
--description DESCRIPTION Description for the VM class (string).
--devices-dynamic-direct-path-io-devices List of Dynamic DirectPath I/O devices (json input).
DEVICES_DYNAMIC_DIRECT_PATH_IO_DEVICES
--devices-vgpu-devices DEVICES_VGPU_DEVICES List of vGPU devices (json input).
--id ID Required. Identifier of the virtual machine class (string).
--instance-storage-policy INSTANCE_STORAGE_POLICY Storage policy corresponding to the instance storage (string).
--instance-storage-volumes INSTANCE_STORAGE_VOLUMES List of instance storage volumes (json input).
--memory-mb MEMORY_MB Required. The amount of memory in MB configured for virtual
machine of this class (integer).
--memory-reservation MEMORY_RESERVATION The percentage of available memory reserved for a virtual
machine of this class.
Use the following examples to create VM classes with different properties.
CPU and Memory
com vmware vcenter namespacemanagement virtualmachineclasses create --id cpu-mem-class --cpu-count 2 --memory-
mb 2048 --config-spec '{"_typeName":"VirtualMachineConfigSpec","numCPUs":2,"memoryMB":2048}'
Setting and in the Config Spec is optional. If you chose to set them, they must have the same values
numCPUs memoryMB
as the mandatory and vAPI fields.
--cpu-count --memory-mb
CPU and Memory Reservations
When you create a VM Class by using a Config Spec having CPU and memory reservation, the memory reservation or
limit is in MB for , MHz for .
memoryAllocation cpuAllocation
com vmware vcenter namespacemanagement virtualmachineclasses create --id cpu-res-class-1 --
config-spec '{"_typeName":"VirtualMachineConfigSpec","numCPUs":2,"memoryMB":2048,"cpuAllocation":
{"_typeName":"ResourceAllocationInfo","reservation":200,"limit":200},"memoryAllocation":
{"_typeName":"ResourceAllocationInfo","reservation":200,"limit":200}}' --cpu-count 2 --memory-mb 2048
Network Adapter
The following command creates a network adapter of type E1000.
com vmware vcenter namespacemanagement virtualmachineclasses create --id class-w-e1000 --cpu-
count 2 --memory-mb 2048 --config-spec '{"_typeName":"VirtualMachineConfigSpec","deviceChange":
[{"_typeName":"VirtualDeviceConfigSpec","operation":"add","device":{"_typeName":"VirtualE1000","key":-100}}]}'

What to do next
The VM classes that you create with the DCLI, become available in vCenter. You can use the vSphere Client to assign
these VM classes to a namespace. See Associate a VM Class with a Namespace Using the vSphere Client.
Deploying a VM with vGPU and Other PCI Devices in a Supervisor
If ESX hosts in your environment have one or more NVIDIA GRID GPU graphics devices, you can configure VMs to use
the NVIDIA GRID virtual GPU (vGPU) technology. You can also configure other PCI devices on an ESX host to make
them available to a VM in a passthrough mode.
Deploying a VM with vGPU in vSphere Supervisor
NVIDIA GRID GPU graphics devices are designed to optimize complex graphics operations and enable them to run
at high performance without overloading the CPU. NVIDIA GRID vGPU provides unparalleled graphics performance,
cost-effectiveness, and scalability by sharing a single physical GPU among multiple VMs as separate vGPU-enabled
passthrough devices.
Considerations
The following considerations apply when you use NVIDIA vGPU:
• Three-zone Supervisor supports VMs with vGPU, but you cannot leave the zone field empty. You must make sure
that the VM and the PV use the same zone. If you deploy a VM without a zone, VM Service places it only by VM class
constraints and might not place it in the same zone as the PV.
– When you create the VM and PVC together in the same manifest, specify the zone in the PVC. For example,
add this annotation:
csi.vsphere.volume-requested-topology: '[{"topology.kubernetes.io/
.
zone":"zone-1"}]'
– When the PV already exists, specify the zone in the VM. The VM needs this label:
topology.kubernetes.io/
.
zone: zone-1
• VMs with vGPU devices that are managed by VM Service are automatically powered off when an ESX host enters
maintenance mode. This might temporarily affect workloads running in the VMs. The VMs are automatically powered
on after the host exists the maintenance mode.
• DRS distributes vGPU VMs in a breadth-first manner across cluster's hosts. For more information, see DRS Placement
of vGPU VMs in the vSphere Resource Management guide.
Requirements
To configure NVIDIA vGPU, follow these requirements:
• Verify that the ESX is supported in the VMware Compatibility Guide, and check with the vendor to verify the host meets
power and configuration requirements.
VMware by Broadcom 381

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
• Configure ESX host graphics settings with at least one device in Shared Direct mode. See Configuring Host Graphics
in the vSphere Resource Management documentation.
• The content library you use for VMs with vGPU devices must include images with the boot mode set to EFI, such as
CentOS.
• Install NVIDIA vGPU software. NVIDIA provides a vGPU software package that includes the following components.
For more information, see appropriate NVIDIA Virtual GPU Software documentation.
– vGPU Manager that a vSphere administrator installs on the ESX host. See VMware Knowledge Base article
2033434.
– Guest VM driver that a DevOps engineer installs in the VM after deploying and booting the VM. See the Install the
NVIDIA Guest Driver in a VM section.

Install the NVIDIA Guest Driver in a VM
If the VM includes a PCI device configured for vGPU, after you create and boot the VM in your environment, install the
NVIDIA vGPU graphics driver to fully enable GPU operations.
• Deploy the VM with vGPU. Make sure that the VM YAML file references the VM class with vGPU definition. See
Deploy a Virtual Machine on a Namespace in Supervisor.
• Verify that you downloaded the vGPU software package from the NVIDIA download site, uncompressed the package,
and have the guest drive component ready. For information, see the appropriate NVIDIA Virtual GPU Software
documentation.
Note:
The version of the driver component must correspond to the version of the vGPU Manager that a vSphere
administrator installed on the host.
1. Copy the NVIDIA vGPU software Linux driver package, for example, version ,
NVIDIA-Linux-x86_64- -grid.run
to the guest VM.
2. Before attempting to run the driver installer, terminate all applications.
3. Start the NVIDIA vGPU driver installer.
version
sudo ./NVIDIA-Linux-x86_64- -grid.run
4. Accept the NVIDIA software license agreement and select Yes to update the X configuration settings automatically.
5. Verify that the driver has been installed.
For example,

Deploying a VM with PCI Devices in Supervisor Environment
In addition to vGPU, you can configure other PCI devices on an host to make them available to a VM in a passthrough
mode.
Supervisor environment supports Dynamic DirectPath I/O devices. Using Dynamic DirectPath I/O, the VM can directly
access the physical PCI and PCIe devices connected to a host. You can use Dynamic DirectPath I/O to assign multiple
PCI passthrough devices to a VM. Each passthrough device can be specified by its PCI vendor and device identifier.
Note:
When configuring Dynamic DirectPath I/O for PCI passthrough devices, connect the PCI devices to the host and
mark them as available for passthrough. See Enable Passthrough for a Network Device on a Host in the vSphere
Networking documentation.
Importing Existing VMs into VM Service
You can bring existing vSphere VMs under Supervisor management so they can be operated through VM Service
and integrated with Kubernetes-based workflows. You can import VMs individually using the vSphere Client. You can
also perform larger, non-disruptive migrations using the API. Both methods transfer the selected VMs into a vSphere
Namespace while preserving their configuration and applying the policies that you specify.
Select one of the following migration methods:
• Individual import using the vSphere Client.
Use this method to import single VMs.
Note:
This operation might disrupt the workload by reconfiguring the VM network identity.
• Batch import using the ImportOperationBatch API.
Use this method for a non-disruptive workflow. By importing using the API, you gain the following capabilities:
• Maintain network identity.
Preserve the original network identity and configuration of the source VMs.
• Preserve placement policies.
Retain existing affinity and anti-affinity placement rules.
• Support snapshots.
Import VMs that contain snapshots.
Import Individual VMs into VM Service
Import an existing VM that runs in your vSphere environment into a namespace on Supervisor, so that this VM can be
managed by VM Service. This operation transfers the VM to Supervisor control while preserving its configuration. Use this
workflow when you want to migrate individual VMs using the vSphere Client.
Required privilege: Namespaces.View, Namespaces.Edit, and VirtualMachine.Supervisor.Transfer.
Note:
Importing VMs using the vSphere Client might disrupt the workload by reconfiguring the VM network identity. For
a non-disruptive import, use this task Import Multiple VMs into VM Service Using ImportOperationBatch.
VMware by Broadcom 386

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
1. In the vSphere Client, navigate to the VM you want to import.
2. Select Migrate from the right-click menu, and select Change Management Layer.
3. Review the VM to be migrated, and click Next.
4. On the Select destination page, select the destination namespace.
5. On the Configure inputs page, select appropriate storage policy, network, and guest OS inputs.
6. Verify that the destination information is correct and click Finish to start the migration.
After the import begins, you can monitor its progress in the vSphere Client and can verify that the VM becomes available
in the destination namespace on the target Supervisor:
• In the vSphere Client, open the Tasks panel to track the migration progress and status.
• If needed, view the corresponding VM resource in a namespace assigned to you by running:
kubectl get
. To access the namespace, see VCF CLI Context, Architecture, and
virtualmachines -n <namespace>
Configuration.
Import Multiple VMs into VM Service Using ImportOperationBatch
You can import multiple VMs from a traditional vSphere environment into a VCF infrastructure and can have these VMs
managed by VM Service. You perform this action by declaratively using an ImportOperationBatch Custom Resource. You
can use this method to transfer multiple VMs at once, apply specific configurations to imported VMs, or control when the
imported VMs become active in the Supervisor environment.
Batch import supports the following capabilities:
• Bulk VM Import
Import one or multiple VMs in a single batch.
• Flexible Storage Selection
Apply the same storage class to all VMs in the batch or specify different storage classes per VM.
• Configurable Commit Behavior
Automate the import completion or wait for manual approval to finalize.
• Automated Rollback
Roll back all VMs in the batch to their original vSphere state if an import is not successful.
To import vSphere VMs, you first create the ImportOperationBatch, a CR where you can define and manage the import of
multiple existing VMs into a Supervisor cluster. You can then apply this CR to the cluster and monitor the progress of the
import using the commands.
kubectl
You typically perform the following steps.
1. Create an ImportOperationBatch CR.
In the YAML file, you define the batch import operation and specify all the source VMs and their target configurations.
The following example shows a batch with basic automatic commit:
apiVersion: mobility-operator.vmware.com/v1alpha3
kind: ImportOperationBatch
metadata:
name: test-batch-auto-commit
namespace: default
spec:
# Default configuration applied to all operations in the batch
defaultSpec:
# Control action with commitAction set to Auto
controlAction:
commitAction: Auto
precheckOnly: false
# Default network mode
mode: preserve
VMware by Broadcom 387

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
# Default storage class
storageClass: "default-storage-class"
# List of 3 import operations for testing
operations:
- name: test-vm-001
spec:
virtualMachineID: "vm-12345"
- name: test-vm-002
spec:
virtualMachineID: "vm-67890"
- name: test-vm-003
spec:
virtualMachineID: "vm-11111"
2. Apply the ImportOperationBatch CR to the cluster.
file
kubectl apply -f .yaml
When the VM Import Operator detects a new or updated resource, it reads the defined state and performs the
necessary actions in the vSphere environment to migrate the specified VMs.
3. Monitor the migration progress.
4. Commit or roll back.
Depending on the commitAction specified in the YAML, the process either completes automatically or waits for a
manual command to finalize or roll back the migration.
Manual Commit and Rollback
If you want to review the batch before committing it, set commitAction to Wait. After the batch reaches the
ReadyForCommit condition, update the resource to commit or roll back the operations.
To roll back the batch instead of committing it, update rollbackAction to Immediate.
apiVersion: mobility-operator.vmware.com/v1alpha3
kind: ImportOperationBatch
metadata:
name: test-batch-rollback
namespace: default
spec:
# Updated configuration to trigger rollback
defaultSpec:
controlAction:
commitAction: Wait
precheckOnly: false
rollbackAction: Immediate # This triggers immediate rollback
mode: preserve
storageClass: "default-storage-class"
# Same operations as before
operations:
- name: test-vm-001
spec:
virtualMachineID: "vm-12345"
- name: test-vm-002
spec:
virtualMachineID: "vm-67890"
- name: test-vm-003
spec:
virtualMachineID: "vm-11111"
VMware by Broadcom 388

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
Specify Different Storage Classes per VM
You can override the default storage class for individual VMs. The operator provisions the target PersistentVolumes using
the storage class specified for each operation.
apiVersion: mobility-operator.vmware.com/v1alpha3
kind: ImportOperationBatch
metadata:
name: test-batch-storage-policies
namespace: default
spec:
# Default configuration applied to all operations in the batch
defaultSpec:
# Control action with commitAction set to Auto
controlAction:
commitAction: Auto
precheckOnly: false
# Default network mode
mode: preserve
# List of 3 import operations with different storage policies per VM
operations:
- name: test-vm-premium-storage
spec:
virtualMachineID: "vm-12345"
# Premium storage policy for this VM
storageClass: "premium-ssd-storage"
- name: test-vm-standard-storage
spec:
virtualMachineID: "vm-67890"
# Standard storage policy for this VM
storageClass: "standard-storage"
- name: test-vm-economy-storage
spec:
virtualMachineID: "vm-11111"
# Economy storage policy for this VM
storageClass: "economy-storage"
Monitor Virtual Machines Available in vSphere Supervisor
As a vSphere administrator, use the vSphere Client to monitor a VM that was deployed by DevOps in the Supervisor
Kubernetes environment.
A DevOps engineer has deployed a VM. See Deploying a Stand-Alone VM in the Environment.
You cannot manage the VM lifecycle from the vSphere Client.
1. In the vSphere Client, navigate to the host cluster that has the Supervisor enabled.
2. Under Namespaces, expand the namespace where a VM was deployed.
3. Select the VM to view and click the Summary tab.
Make sure that you see the Developer Managed tag at the top of the Summary page.
The page displays information about the VM, including its guest OS and IP addresses.

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
Installing and Configuring the Argo CD Service in VCF and
vSphere
As a VI administrator or a provider administrator, you can now deploy Argo CD in your VCF environment to provide
declarative GitOps continuous delivery to your workloads running on vSphere Namespaces and VKS clusters.
Argo CD is a centralized service for installing and managing Argo CD instance in your environment. It leverages the Argo
CD operator to deploy and manage Argo CD instances. You install Argo CD instances in a vSphere Namespaces to
enable managing workloads in vSphere Namespaces and VKS clusters.
Two options exist for deploying, configuring, and managing Argo CD in VCF:
• Install and configure Argo CD as a Supervisor Service on individual Supervisor instances.
• Install Argo CD as a regional VCF service by using VCF Automation.
Install Argo CD as VCF Service in VCF Automation
Install the Argo CD VCF Service in VCF Automation to control how the Argo CD Supervisor Service is deployed across all
Supervisors that are registered in VCF Automation.
• Verify that the VCF Download Tool is installed and configured. For installation instructions, see Installing the VCF
Download Tool. For CLI usage, see the VCF Download Tool command reference.
1. Use the VCF Download Tool to download the Argo CD Service tarball locally.
# vcf-download-tool artifacts download --vcf-version=<vcf version> --depot-download-activation-code-
file=<active_code_file> --component=VCF_SERVICE_ARGOCD --depot-store=<the local directory to store
download files>
After this command, you can get the tarball from local path:
./depot-store/PROD/COMP/VCF_SERVICE_ARGOCD/
The following table describes the command options.
Option Description
--vcf-version The VCF version of your environment.
--depot-download-activation-code-file Path to a text file containing a single line with your activation code.
--component Use VCF_SERVICE_ARGOCD to download the required tarball
for installation.
--depot-store The directory to store the downloaded files.
The example output of the download command:
# vcf-download-tool artifacts download --vcf-version=9.1.1 --depot-download-activation-code-
file=activation-code.txt --component=VCF_SERVICE_ARGOCD --depot-store=./depot-store
......

The Argo CD service is installed. The Argo CD Supervisor Service is deployed across all Supervisors that are registered
in VCF Automation.
Install the VMware Argo CD Operator as a Supervisor Service
Learn how to install and configure the VMware Argo CD Operator on the Supervisor. The Argo CD Supervisor Service
is a Broadcom developed Kubernetes Operator to manage the life cycle of Argo CD instances. You deploy the VMware
Argo CD Operator on the Supervisor and then install an Argo CD instance in a vSphere Namespace so that you can use
to manage workloads in vSphere Namespaces and VKS clusters.
• Upgrade to Supervisor release 9.0.0.0100 which includes support for Supervisor version 1.30.10. See Update the
Supervisor.
• For vSphere 8, upgrade to vSphere 8.0 Update 3g.
1. Download the Argo CD Operator YAML definition and the customized Argo CD CLI from the Broadcom support portal.
2. Install Argo CD service on a Supervisor.
See Install a Supervisor Service on a Supervisor
Deploying an Argo CD Instance
An Argo CD instance is a declarative, production-ready deployment of ArgoCD managed by a dedicated Kubernetes
operator in vSphere and VCF. Understanding the two available deployment modes helps you select the correct
configuration for your environment before you deploy Argo CD.
What is an Argo CD Instance?
An Argo CD instance is managed through the Argo CD custom resource (CR), which belongs to the API group
argocd-
. Platform administrators and developers use the ArgoCD CR to deploy
service.vsphere.vmware.com/v1alpha1
and manage Argo CD in a vSphere Namespace.
VMware by Broadcom 392

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
When you create or update an ArgoCD custom resource, the operator automatically provisions, configures, and manages
the lifecycle of the underlying Kubernetes workloads and resources inside the specified vSphere Namespace. The
operator actively reconciles and controls the core components of the Argo CD instance to prevent configuration drift. For a
full list of controlled resources, see Custom Resource Reference.
Argo CD Service Deployment Modes
Two modes exist for deploying an Argo CD instance - VCF Automation mode where you deploy Argo CD as a VCF
service, and Supervisor Service mode where you deploy Argo CD on individual Supervisors. Both modes deploy the same
core Argo CD workloads. They differ in how they handle user authentication, platform identity, and role bindings.
Attribute VCF Automation Supervisor Service
Primary use case Multi-tenant environments that are vSphere environments without VCF
managed by VCF Automation. Automation.
Authentication and SSO OIDC integrated by default (single sign-on). Kubernetes RBAC and local accounts
(standard password). You must configure
OIDC manually.
Platform identity Auto-provisions a platform-level VCF No platform-level service account. Auto-
Automation service account. provisions a local Kubernetes service
account.
Role binding and authorization Platform-level role binding. Manually bind Namespace-level role binding. Manually
the Argo CD instance role to the VCF create a RoleBinding inside the target
Automation service account in the VCF namespace to authorize the local
Automation provider UI. Kubernetes service account.
Deploying and Managing an Argo CD Instance as a VCF Service in VCF
Automation
Learn how to deploy and manage an Argo CD instance when Argo CD is deployed as a regional VCF Service in VCF
Automation. Explore how to deploy an Argo CD instance, register a namespace as a target cluster in the Argo CD
instance, register and deploy VKS clusters, vSphere Pods, and VMs.
Deploy an Argo CD Instance by Using the VCF Automation organization UI
Learn how to deploy an Argo CD instance in VCF Automation in your assigned organization and project.
• Verify that a target VCF Automation project and namespace are created and configured.
1. Log in to the VCF Automation organization as an organization administrator.
2. Select Build & Deploy.
3. Under Services, select GitOps.
4. Click Create Argo CD Instance.
5. Provide basic configuration for Argo CD instance.
Property Value
Argo CD Name Enter a name for the Argo CD instance.
Project Select a project from the ones assigned to you account where to
place the Argo CD instance.
Version Select from the compatible versions.
Optional Controllers Optional. Select one or both options:
• Application Set Controller
• Notification Controller
VMware by Broadcom 393

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
Property Value
Argo CD FQDN Enter an external domain name or FQDN for the Argo CD
instance, where you will be able to access the Argo CD UI portal.
If you skip this field, you can access the Argo CD UI through an IP
address.
Server-side Diff Leave enabled. This setting is required so that the Argo CD
instance can manage VKS clusters in vSphere Namespaces.
TLS Cert Configuration Provide the details for the TLS certificate.
6. Click Next.
7. Optional. Configure OIDC and RBAC policies for the users of the Argo CD instance.
If you select not to use the VCF Automation OIDC, you must provide that configuration manually. You can configure
RBAC policies after the Argo CD instance in deployed.
8. Review the settings and click Create Argo CD Instance.
Once the Argo CD instance is deployed, it's status changes to Success. You can click the instance in the able to view it's
configuration.
Manage an Argo CD Instance by Using VCF Automation organization UI
Learn how to maintain an Argo CD instance by using the VCF Automation oragnizaiton UI by updating its configuration,
upgrading to a newer supported version, or deleting the instance and cleaning up its resources.
Change the Argo CD Instance Basic Deployment Configuration
1. In the VCF Automation organization UI, select Build & Deploy and select GitOps.
2. Click the Argo CD instance from the table.
3. In Argo CD Instance Details, click Edit.
You can change the following configuration settings:
Option Description
Version Change the Argo CD version from the list of supported versions.
Optional Controllers Change the configuration for the application set and notification
controllers.
Argo Server FQDN Set a domain name to access the Argo CD UI portal.
Server-side Diff Enable or disable this setting.
TLS cert configuration Provide the details for a TLS certificate.
Configure User Access for the Argo CD Instance
To configure access of user accounts to the Argo CD instance:
1. Next Global RBAC, click Edit.
2. Enter users and assign them a role.
Configure Resources to the Argo CD Instance
In the Resources tab, you can set the resource limits for the Argo CD instance.
Delete the Argo CD Instance
1. In the VCF Automation organization UI, select Build & Deploy and select GitOps.
2. Click the Argo CD instance from the table.
3. Click the three dots next to the Argo CD instance and select Delete.
VMware by Broadcom 394

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
Deploy an Argo CD Instance in VCF Automation by Using VCF CLI
Use the plugin to declaratively create, retrieve, update, upgrade, and delete an Argo CD instance in VCF
vcf argocd
Automation.
• Verify that a target VCF Automation project and namespace are created and configured.
1. Log in and switch to the active context.
Log in through VCF CLI and switch to the namespace-scoped CCI context corresponding to your target namespace
and project.
vcf context create vcfa --endpoint <vcfa_url> --type cci --tenant-name <vcfa_org>
vcf context use vcfa-context:argocd-ns-6n8ql:argocd-project
Note:
All subsequent VCF CLI commands operate within the active context’s namespace and project.
2. Search for and install the plug-in for the VCF CLI.
argocd
vcf plugin search --name argocd
vcf plugin install argocd
3. Deploy a minimal Argo CD instance.
a) Query the available versions that support an installation.
vcf argocd instance versions
Output:
VERSION DESCRIPTION
3.4.4+vmware.1-vks.1 Recommended version.
3.3.12+vmware.1-vks.1 Recommended version.
3.2.12+vmware.1-vks.1 For upgrade support only.
3.1.16+vmware.1-vks.1 For upgrade support only.
b) Prepare the minimal Argo CD manifest.
Create a file named with the minimal configuration by replacing the version with
argocd-instance.yaml
veresion that you retrieved in the previous step.
apiVersion: argocd-service.vsphere.vmware.com/v1alpha1
kind: ArgoCD
metadata:
name: argocd-1
spec:
version: "3.4.4+vmware.1-vks.1"
c) Apply the manifest to create the Argo CD instance.
vcf argocd instance create -f argocd-instance.yaml
Note:
After creation is initiated, the CLI automatically attempts to bind the required roles to the Argo CD instance service
account. If you do not have permission to bind roles, a warning is displayed, but the instance creation continues.
Output:

get instance status.

4. Verify, inspect, and log in to the Argo CD instance.
a) Verify that the Argo CD instance is created and check its status.
vcf argocd instance list
Output:

vcf argocd instance get
To filter by project and namespace and retrieve instance information in another namespace, with JSON output:
vcf argocd instance get --vcfa-project my-project --vsphere-namespace my-namespace -o json
c) Retrieve the load balancer IP or URL from the column of the instance list output or from the
SERVER vcf argocd
field in the detailed YAML.
status.externalIP
d) Select a login method.
Method Description
Log in through OIDC (recommended) If OIDC is not configured in the Argo CD instance YAML, the a
rgocd-service automatically configures the VCFA OIDC
integration. This allows you to log in directly by using your VCF
Automation credentials.
Run the login command with the --sso flag:
vcf argocd login 192.168.130.6 --sso
This command opens your default Web browser, or provides a
URL, to authenticate by using your VCF Automation credentials.
Log in through the default admin account Retrieve the auto-generated password:
kubectl get secret argocd-initial-admin-secret -o
jsonpath='{.data.password}' | base64 -d
Then log in interactively:

Provide the user name admin and paste the decoded password.
e) Update the default admin password immediately after logging in.
vcf argocd account update-password
f) After logging in to the Argo CD server, verify the server version.
vcf argocd server-version
Note:
This command is renamed from the upstream version to server-version to avoid a conflict with the VCF CLI plug-
in’s built-in version command.
Maintaining the Argo CD Instance in VCF Automation by Using VCF CLI
Learn how to maintain an Argo CD instance in VCF Automation by updating its configuration, upgrading to a newer
supported version, or deleting the instance and cleaning up its resources.
Update the Argo CD Configuration
Add features such as local user accounts, custom RBAC policies, or theApplicationSet controller by modifying your local
configuration manifest and applying it.
For example, to add local accounts and enable the ApplicationSet controller:
VMware by Broadcom 396

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
apiVersion: argocd-service.vsphere.vmware.com/v1alpha1
kind: ArgoCD
metadata:
name: argocd-1
spec:
version: "3.4.4+vmware.1-vks.1"
localAccounts:
- developer-01
- operator-02
applicationSet:
enabled: true
Apply the updated configuration:
vcf argocd instance apply -f argocd-instance.yaml
Upgrade the Argo CD version
To upgrade the instance to a newer supported version, run the command with the target version:
upgrade
vcf argocd instance upgrade argocd-1 --version 3.4.4+vmware.1-vks.1
Note:
Add the flag to skip the confirmation prompt in automation scripts.
-y or --yes
Remove the Argo CD instance
To tear down the Argo CD deployment and clean up its resources..
vcf argocd instance delete argocd-1
Note:
Add the flag to skip the confirmation prompt.
-y or --yes

Use kubectl to declaratively create, retrieve, update, upgrade, and delete an Argo CD instance in a vSphere Namespace
under VCF Service (VCF Automation mode).
• Verify that the Argo CD VCF Service is successfully installed and running in your environment.
• Verify that a target vSphere Namespace, for example, , is created, configured, and associated with
argocd-ns-6n8ql
a VCF Automation project.
• Verify that the VCF CLI is installed on your client machine.
For the complete OpenAPI specification and schema reference for this custom resource, see the Argo CD Service API
Reference.
1. Search for and install the plug-in for the VCF CLI.
argocd
vcf plugin search --name argocd
vcf plugin install argocd
2. Log in and switch to the active context.
Log in through VCF CLI and switch to the namespace-scoped CCI context corresponding to your target namespace
and project.
vcf context create vcfa --endpoint <vcfa_url> --type cci --tenant-name <vcfa_org>
vcf context use vcfa-context:argocd-ns-6n8ql:argocd-project

3. Deploy a minimal Argo CD instance.
a) Query the supported versions.
The operator automatically manages a list of supported Argo CD versions in a cluster-scoped Argo CD Version
resource. Query this resource to retrieve the supported versions.
kubectl get argocdversion argocd-supported-versions -o jsonpath='{.spec.versions}' | jq

b) Prepare the minimal Argo CD manifest with custom RBAC.
Under the VCF Service, the VCF Automation OIDC is integrated by default, which means user authentication
through VCF Automation is automatically configured for single sign-on (SSO).
To provide the authenticated users full access to manage applications, configure the field to assign
spec.rbac
to specific logged-in users by email or username or corporate groups.
role:admin
Create a file named with the following confguration, targeting your namespace and by
argocd-instance.yaml
using a version retrieved inthe previous step:
apiVersion: argocd-service.vsphere.vmware.com/v1alpha1
kind: ArgoCD
metadata:
name: argocd-1
namespace: argocd-ns-6n8ql
spec:
version: "3.4.4+vmware.1-vks.1"
rbac:
policy: |
# Assign role:admin to the authenticated user's email/username or group
g, fritz, role:admin
g, serviceadministrator, role:admin
g, bob@sqa.vcfa.broadcom.net, role:admin
c) Deploy the Argo CD instance by applying the manifest to your target namespace.
kubectl apply -f argocd-instance.yaml -n argocd-ns-6n8ql

Maintaining the Argo CD in VCF Automation Instance by Using kubectl
Learn how to maintain an Argo CD instance in VCF Automation by updating its configuration, upgrading to a newer
supported version, or deleting the instance and cleaning up its resources by using kubectl.
VMware by Broadcom 401

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
Updating the Argo CD Configuration
Add features such as local user accounts, custom RBAC policy engines, or the controller by modifying
ApplicationSet
your local confguration manifest and applying it.
For example, to add local accounts and enable the controller:
ApplicationSet
apiVersion: argocd-service.vsphere.vmware.com/v1alpha1
kind: ArgoCD
metadata:
name: argocd-1
namespace: argocd-ns-6n8ql
spec:
version: "3.4.4+vmware.1-vks.1"
localAccounts:
- developer-01
- operator-02
applicationSet:
enabled: true
Apply the updated configuration:
kubectl apply -f argocd-instance.yaml -n argocd-ns-6n8ql
Upgrade the Argo CD Version
To upgrade the instance to a newer supported version, update the version field in the manifest or apply a merge patch
directly:
kubectl patch argocd argocd-1 -n argocd-ns-6n8ql --type='merge' -p '{"spec":{"version":"3.4.4+vmware.1-
vks.1"}}'
The operator orchestrates a rolling update of the underlying pods to the new version with minimal downtime.
Delete the Argo CD Instance
To delete the Argo CD deployment and clean up its resources:
kubectl delete argocd argocd-1 -n argocd-ns-6n8ql
The custom resource uses finalizer mechanisms to ensure graceful cleanup. The operator automatically uninstalls the
underlying package and terminates the core workloads - including deployments, StatefulSets, services, and configurations
- inside the namespace, preventing orphaned components.
What to do Next
Register a vSphere Namespace or VKS cluster with the Argo CD instance. See Managing VKS Clusters in Argo CD with
VCF Automation.

UI
Learn how to register, verify, update, and deregister a target namespace as a managed cluster in an Argo CD instance
running on VCF Automation by using the VCF Automation organization UI. When running under VCF Automation,
registering a target namespace is fully automated.
VMware by Broadcom 402

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
Register a Namespace as a Target Cluster in Argo CD
1. In the VCF Automation organization UI, select Buid&Deploy and select GitOps.
2. Click the Argo CD instance from the table and select Scope.
3. Under vSphere Namespaces, click Attach Namespace.
4. Select a project where the namespace is located.
5. Select a namespace from the list and click Attach.
The namespace appears on the list and it takes certian time so that it is added as a target cluster in Argo CD. On once the
namespace is attached to the Argo CD instance, all the workloads that are running in the namespace, such as vSphere
Pods, VKS clusters, and VMs become available for management through this Argo CD instance.
Remove a Namespace from an Argo CD Instance
1. Click the Argo CD instance from the table and select Scope.
2. Click the three dots next to the namespace that you want to remove.
3. Select Remove.

Prerequisites

where your Argo CD instance is running.

All subsequent vcf instance commands operate within the active context’s namespace and project.

Register a vSphere Namespace
1. Register the target vSphere Namespace.
To register a target vSphere Namespace to your Argo CD instance, run the command, specifying the
add-cluster
target vSphere Namespace and its corresponding VCF Automation project.
vcf argocd instance add-cluster --vsphere-namespace target-namespace --vcfa-project target-project
The following optional flags are available at registration time:
Flag Description
--display-name Overwrites the default cluster display name inArgo CD.
--project Assigns the cluster to a specific Argo CD project.
--namespace Not required. For VKS clusters only.
--proxy-url Uses a proxy to connect to the target cluster.
--disable-compression Bypasses automatic GZip compression requests to the server.
If you run the command without the or flag, you are prompted to confrm the operation:
-y --yes
Will add vSphere namespace: target-namespace, project: target-project. Do you want to
continue [y/N]? y

Update a Registered vSphere Namespace Cluster in Argo CD
Important:
The target reference of a registered cluster is immutable. You cannot update an existing registration to point to a
different vSphere Namespace. To manage a different namespace, register it as a new cluster.
To update other configuration parameters of a registered cluster, for example, to change the cluster display name in Argo
CD, run the following command:
vcf argocd instance update-cluster target-namespace-target-proj --display-name custom-display-name
To reset all custom configurations, such as display name and managed namespaces, back to defaults, run the command
without additional flags:
vcf argocd instance update-cluster target-namespace-target-proj

rm-cluster
registered name:

Manage a vSphere Namespace in Argo CD by Using kubectl in VCF Automation
Learn how to register, update, and delete a target vSphere Namespace as a managed cluster in an Argo CD instance on
a VCF service by using kubectl in VCF Automation.
For the complete OpenAPI specification and schema reference for this custom resource, see the Argo CD Service API
Reference.
Prerequisites
• Complete the steps in Deploy an Argo CD Instance in VCF Automation by Using kubectl to create an Argo CD instance
before you register a namespace.
Register a vSphere Namespace in Argo CD
1. Bind the role to the VCF Automation service account.
ArgoCD Instance
When you deploy or update an Argo CD instance using kubectl, the operator automatically provisions a platform-level
VCF Automation service account. No automatic role binding is performed.
To allow the service account to communicate with VCF Automation APIs and fetch namespace connection details, you
must manually bind the platform-level role to this service account. You can perform this step if
ArgoCD Instance
you have Organization Administrator permissions, or an OrganizationAdministrator can perform it for you.
a. Retrieve the service account name from your Argo CD CR status:
kubectl get argocd argocd-1 -n argocd-ns-6n8ql -o jsonpath='{.status.serviceAccounts.platform.name}'
b. Log in to the VCF Automation portal as an Organization Administrator.
a. Navigate to Adminiter > Access Control > Service Accounts
c. Locate the service account matching the name retrieved in step 1.
d. Edit the role configuration and assign the ArgoCD Instance role to the service account.
2. Create the ManagedEntity resource.
Create a custom resource in the Argo CD namespace. This resource points to your target
ManagedEntity
namespace. The project field is required under the Argo CD VCF service.
a. Create a file named :
managedentity-namespace.yaml
apiVersion: argocd-service.vsphere.vmware.com/v1alpha1
kind: ManagedEntity
metadata:
name: target-ns-registration
namespace: argocd-ns-6n8ql # Must be the namespace where your ArgoCD is deployed
spec:
targetRef:
apiGroup: ""
kind: Namespace
name: vks-ns-p74qz # The target vSphere namespace
project: argocd-project # REQUIRED: The VCF Automation project name
b. Apply the resource.
kubectl apply -f managedentity-namespace.yaml -n argocd-ns-6n8ql
Verify Registration Status
1. Inspect the status and phase of your
ManagedEntity:
kubectl get me -n argocd-ns-6n8ql

AGE

ac3dd594c7b0 3h27m

ManagedEntity

Managing VKS Clusters in Argo CD with VCF Automation
Learn how to manage VKS clusters in your namespace by using Argo CD.
Manage a VKS Cluster in Argo CD by Using the VCF Automation organization UI
Learn how to register and unregister an existing VKS cluster as a managed target cluster in an Argo CD instance by using
the VCF Automation organization UI.
Prerequisites
• Create an Argo CD instance.
• Attach a namespace as a target cluster in the Argo CD instance.
Register a VKS Cluster in Argo CD
You can attach VKS clusters that are avaialble in the project where you Argo CD instance is running.
1. In the VCF Automation organization UI, select Buid&Delploy and select GitOps.
2. Select the Argo CD instance and select Scope.
3. Under Kubernetes Clusters, select Attach Kubernetes Cluster.
4. Select a project, and select a target VKS cluster.
5. Click Attach.
The target VKS cluster will be attached and available for management by this Argo CD instnace.
Remove a VKS Cluster in Argo CD
1. Select the Argo CD instance and select Scope.
2. Under Kubernetes Clusters, click the three dots next to the cluster that you want to remove, and select Remove.

Register a VKS Cluster
1. Register the target VKS cluster.
To register a target VKS cluster to your Argo CD instance, run the add-cluster command. Specify the target VKS
cluster name, the hosting vSphere Namespace, and the corresponding VCF Automation project.
vcf argocd instance add-cluster --vsphere-namespace hosting-namespace --vcfa-project target-project --vks-
cluster target-vks
To host specific namespaces in the VKS cluster, add the --namespace flag for each namespace.
vcf argocd instance add-cluster --vsphere-namespace hosting-namespace --vcfa-project target-project --vks-
cluster target-vks --namespace ns1 --namespace ns2
The following optional flags are available at registration time.
Flag Description
--display-name Overwrites the default cluster display name in Argo CD.
--project Assigns the cluster to a specific Argo CD project.
--namespace Lists specific namespaces allowed to be managed. Can be
specified multiple times.
--proxy-url Uses a proxy to connect to the target cluster.
--disable-compression Bypasses automatic GZip compression requests to the server.

Manage VKS Clusters in an Argo CD Instance on VCF Service by Using kubectl
Learn how to register, update, and delete a VKS cluster as a managed target cluster in an Argo CD instance running on
VCF service by using kubectl.
For the complete OpenAPI specification and schema reference for this custom resource, see the Argo CD Service API
Reference.
Prerequisite
• The automatically created VCF Automation service account of your Argo CD instance must have the platform-level
ArgoCD Instance role assigned.
VMware by Broadcom 412

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
• You must specify the target VKS cluster name, the hosting vSphere Namespace, and the project field in the
registration. The project field is the VCF Automation project where the cluster belongs.
• Complete the steps in Deploy an Argo CD Instance in VCF Automation by Using kubectl to create an Argo CD instance
before you register a VKS cluster.
Register a VKS Cluster
1. Bind the ArgoCD Instance role to the VCF Automation service account.
When you deploy or update an Argo CD instance by using kubectl, the operator automatically provisions a platform-
level VCF Automation service account. No automatic role binding is performed.
To allow the service account to communicate with the VCF Automation APIs and fetch VKS cluster connection details,
you must manually bind the platform-level role to this service account. You can perform this step
ArgoCD Instance
if you have Organization Administrator permissions, or an Organization Administrator can perform it for you.
a. Retrieve the service account name from your Argo CD CR status.
kubectl get argocd argocd-1 -n argocd-ns-6n8ql -o jsonpath='{.status.serviceAccounts.platform.name}'
b. Log in to the VCF Automation portal as an Organization Administrator.
c. Navigate to Administer > Access Control > Service Accounts.
d. Locate the service account matching the name retrieved in step 1.
e. Edit the role configuration and assign the ArgoCD Instance role to the service account.
2. Create a custom resource in the Argo CD namespace.
ManagedEntity
This resource points to your target VKS cluster. The project field is required under the VCF Service.
a. Create a file named .
managedentity-vks.yaml
apiVersion: argocd-service.vsphere.vmware.com/v1alpha1
kind: ManagedEntity

Deploying and Managing an Argo CD Instance as a Supervisor Service
Learn how to deploy and manage an Argo CD instance on individual Supervisors as a Supervisor Service without VCF
Automation.
Deploy an Argo CD Instance on a Supervisor without VCF Automation
Learn how to declaratively create, retrieve, update, upgrade, and delete an Argo CD instance in a vSphere Namespace on
a Supervisor without VCF Automation.
For the complete OpenAPI specification and schema reference for this custom resource, see the Argo CD Service API
Reference.
Prerequisites
• Verify that the Argo CD Supervisor Service is installed and running on the Supervisor.
• Verify that a target vSphere Namespace (for example, is created and configured. You must have the
argocd-1)
embedded ClusterRole or another self-defined ClusterRole assigned to your user or group on this namespace.
edit
Configure this permission through the vSphere Client namespace permissions to authorize deploying Kubernetes
resources.
• Log in and switch to the active context, log in through VCF CLI:
vcf context create mgmt-cluster --endpoint <endpoint IP address> --type k8s
Note:
All subsequent kubectl commands operate within the active context's namespace and project.

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
Update Argo CD Configurations
Add features such as local user accounts, custom RBAC policy engines, or the ApplicationSet controller by modifying your
local configuration manifest and applying it.
For example, to add local accounts and enable the ApplicationSet controller:
apiVersion: argocd-service.vsphere.vmware.com/v1alpha1
kind: ArgoCD
metadata:
name: argocd-1
namespace: argocd-1
spec:
version: "3.4.4+vmware.1-vks.1"
localAccounts:
- developer-01
- operator-02
applicationSet:
enabled: true
Apply the updated configuration:
kubectl apply -f argocd-instance.yaml -n argocd-1
Upgrade the Argo CD Version
To upgrade the instance to a newer supported version, update the version field in the manifest or apply a merge patch
directly:
kubectl patch argocd argocd-1 -n argocd-1 --type='merge' -p '{"spec":{"version":"3.4.4+vmware.1-vks.1"}}'
The operator orchestrates a rolling update of the underlying pods to the new version with minimal downtime.
Remove the Argo CD Instance
To tear down the Argo CD deployment and clean up its resources:
kubectl delete argocd argocd-1 -n argocd-1
The custom resource uses finalizer mechanisms to ensure graceful cleanup. The operator automatically uninstalls
the underlying package and terminates the core workloads — including deployments, StatefulSets, services, and
configurations — inside the namespace, preventing orphaned components.

Recommendation Summary
To select the optimal topology for your environment, use the following guidelines that are based on the number of target
vSphere Namespaces:
Namespaces Recommendation
Fewer than 15 vSphere Namespaces • Recommendation: Approach 1 (Standalone Multi-Cluster) is
highly suitable.
• Sizing: A single controller replica (spec.controller.replicas: 1)
handles the load without extra configuration.
15 to 50 vSphere Namespaces • Option A (Approach 1): Continue using Approach 1, but
scale out the controller by increasing the replicas to at least 3
(spec.controller.replicas: 3) to distribute the connection load.
• Option B (Approach 2): If resource optimization is a priority, or
to avoid scaling out replicas, adopt Approach 2 (High-Density
Multi-Namespace).

above 15 namespaces Namespace) is strongly recommended.

1) remains sufficient. Scale only the CPU and memory limits
of this single replica based on the actual size and number of
deployed Argo CD Applications.

Approach 1: Add and Manage a vSphere Namespace in an Argo CD Instance on Supervisor
Service by Using kubectl
Learn how to register, update, and delete a target vSphere Namespace as a managed cluster in an Argo CD instance
running on a Supervisor by using kubectl.
For the complete OpenAPI specification and schema reference for this custom resource, see the Argo CD Service API
Reference.
Prerequisites
• Deploy an Argo CD instance on the Supervisor. See Deploy an Argo CD Instance on a Supervisor without VCF
Automation
Register a vSphere Namespace
1. Authorize the Argo CD service account.
Create a RoleBinding inside the target vSphere Namespace. This authorizes the Argo CD instance service account,
from the Argo CD namespace, to manage resources in the target namespace.
argocd-k8s-sa
a. Create a file named .
argocd-target-binding.yaml
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
name: argocd-access-binding
namespace: test-1 # The target vSphere namespace to be managed
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
name: argocd-k8s-sa
namespace: argocd-1 # The namespace where your ArgoCD is deployed
roleRef:
apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
kind: ClusterRole
name: edit # Grants edit access. Use a custom role or 'edit' depending on your security policy
b. Apply the binding to the target namespace.
kubectl apply -f argocd-target-binding.yaml -n test-1
Note:
If this RoleBinding is missing, the registration fails with a error.
MissingRoleBinding
2. Create the resource.
ManagedEntity
Create a ManagedEntity custom resource in the Argo CD namespace. This resource points to the target namespace.
a. Create a file named .
managedentity-namespace.yaml
apiVersion: argocd-service.vsphere.vmware.com/v1alpha1
kind: ManagedEntity
metadata:
name: target-ns-registration
namespace: argocd-1 # Must be the namespace where your ArgoCD is deployed
spec:
targetRef:
apiGroup: ""
kind: Namespace
name: test-1 # The target vSphere namespace
b. Apply the resource.
kubectl apply -f managedentity-namespace.yaml -n argocd-1

Register and Manage VKS Clusters in an Argo CD Instance on Supervisor
Service by Using kubectl
Register, update, and delete a VKS cluster as a managed target cluster in an Argo CD instance running on a Supervisor
by using kubectl without VCF Automation.
For the complete OpenAPI specification and schema reference for this custom resource, see the Argo CD Service API
Reference.
Prerequisites
• Complete the steps in Deploy an Argo CD Instance on a Supervisor without VCF Automation to create an Argo CD
instance.
• Verify that the Argo CD CLI is installed and that you are logged in to your Argo CD instance.
Register a VKS Cluster
1. Authorize the Argo CD service account.
The controller fetches the VKS cluster connection secrets by using the
ManagedEntity argocd-k8s-sa service
account identity. The service account must have read access to the VKS cluster objects and secrets inside the
vSphere namespace hosting the VKS cluster (for example, test-1).
– Option A: Reuse an existing RoleBinding (no action needed).
If you have already registered the hosting vSphere namespace as a target managed cluster, a RoleBinding
test-1
granting edit or admin permissions to already exists in . Because edit permissions
argocd-k8s-sa test-1
include read access to clusters and secrets, no additional is needed. Proceed directly to Step 2.
RoleBinding
– Option B: Least-privilege RoleBinding (VKS management only)
If you use this Argo CD instance only for VKS cluster management and do not want to manage the hosting vSphere
Namespace itself, bind the service account to the pre-defined least-privilege ClusterRole .
argocd-manage-vks
The Supervisor Service automatically installs this ClusterRole. It allows only retrieving VKS cluster objects and
credentials.
a. Create a file named argocd-vks-hosting-binding.yaml.
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
name: argocd-vks-access-binding
namespace: test-1 # The target hosting vSphere namespace
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
name: argocd-k8s-sa
namespace: argocd-1 # The namespace where your ArgoCD is deployed
roleRef:
apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
kind: ClusterRole
name: argocd-manage-vks # Pre-created, least-privilege ClusterRole
b. Apply the binding.
kubectl apply -f argocd-vks-hosting-binding.yaml -n test-1

Autoattaching VKS Clusters to an Argo CD Instance with the Argo CD Supervisor
Service
Learn how to configure an custom resource so that the Argo CD service automatically
EntityManagementPolicy
discovers, registers, and manages VKS clusters on a Supervisor without manual registration. By defining declarative rules
in the policy, the service provisions and configures resources that register matching VKS clusters to
ManagedEntity
Argo CD.
Overview
The Entity Auto Management feature automates the registration of VKS clusters into Argo CD. Platform administrators
and DevOps operators define declarative rules in an custom resource. The Argo CD
EntityManagementPolicy
Service evaluates these rules continuously, matches target VKS clusters, and automatically provisions
ManagedEntity
resources that register the matched clusters into Argo CD.
For the complete OpenAPI specification and schema reference for the custom resource,
EntityManagementPolicy
see the Argo CD Service API Reference.
How the VKS Autoattach System Works
The controller continuously evaluates active policies. When a VKS cluster matches a policy, reaches a Ready state, and
passes validation, the service automatically generates a matching ManagedEntity resource and an Argo CD registration
secret [2].
The workflow follows these stages:
VMware by Broadcom 427

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
• Policy definition. You create an in the same namespace as the Argo CD instance. The
EntityManagementPolicy
policy contains rules that select target VKS clusters and a configuration template.
• Cluster matching. The controller evaluates the policy rules against VKS clusters on the Supervisor. A cluster matches
when it satisfies the namespace, name, label, and Common Expression Language (CEL) selectors defined in the
policy.
• Resource provisioning. For each matched cluster, the service creates a resource and an Argo CD
ManagedEntity
registration secret that registers the cluster into Argo CD.
• Continuous reconciliation. The controller monitors changes to policies and target clusters, and updates the generated
resources accordingly.
EntityManagementPolicy
An is a custom resource that defines the rules and configuration for automatic cluster
EntityManagementPolicy
management. The policy resides in the same namespace as the Argo CD instance. Each policy contains:
• An enabled field that activates or deactivates the policy.
• A list of rules that select target VKS clusters by namespace, name, label, and CEL expression.
• A configuration template that applies labels, annotations, proxy settings, and project association to the generated
and Argo CD secret.
ManagedEntity
ManagedEntity
A is an auto-generated resource that represents a registered VKS cluster. The policy controller creates
ManagedEntity
a for each matched cluster by using a deterministic naming convention. The generated resource
ManagedEntity
includes tracking labels and annotations that identify the creating and managing policies
Argo CD Registration Secrets
The generated automatically provisions an Argo CD registration secret. This secret contains the
ManagedEntity
credentials and endpoint information that Argo CD uses to communicate with the registered cluster. The secret inherits the
labels and annotations defined in the policy configuration template.
VKS Cluster Readiness Gate
Argo CD does not generate a or an Argo CD registration secret until the target VKS cluster reaches
ManagedEntity
a Ready state on the Supervisor. The registration occurs automatically upon cluster readiness. After you create an
, the service evaluates all ready clusters and creates resources for the
EntityManagementPolicy ManagedEntity
clusters that match the rules.
Policy Precedence and Conflict Resolution
Only one can represent a discovered VKS cluster in a namespace. If multiple active policies target the
ManagedEntity
same VKS cluster, the system applies a deterministic resolution mechanism:
• First-created policy precedence. The system evaluates the creation timestamps (. )
metadata.creationTimestamp
of all matching policies. The earliest created policy is selected to manage the VKS cluster.
• Conflict reporting. Non-precedent policies are not applied. Instead, they report a conflict status for that target in their
list with the outcome .
status.decisions EligibleButNotManaged
Create an EntityManagementPolicy for VKS Cluster Auto Management
Create an custom resource to automatically discover, register, and manage VKS clusters
EntityManagementPolicy
on a Tanzu Supervisor in the Argo CD Supervisor Service.
• Verify that you have access to a Supervisor with the Argo CD Supervisor Service installed and running.
• Verify that an An Argo CD instance is deployed and running in a dedicated vSphere Namespace.
• Verify that you have permissions to create VKS clusters in the API group in every vSphere
cluster.x-k8s.io
Namespace that you specify in the policy list. If you don't have
spec.rules[*].namespaces.nameSelector
VMware by Broadcom 428

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
sufficient privileges in any of the target namespaces, the admission validator rejects the creation or update of the
policy.
• Get informed about the vSphere Namespace of your Argo CD instance. You must create the
resource in the same namespace as the Argo CD instance.
EntityManagementPolicy
1. Create a YAML manifest file for the resource with the policy rules and configuration
EntityManagementPolicy
template.
apiVersion: argocd-service.vsphere.vmware.com/v1alpha1
kind: EntityManagementPolicy
metadata:
name: dev-vks-auto-policy
namespace: argocd-1 # Same namespace as your Argo CD instance
spec:
# Enable or disable the policy. Default is true.
enabled: true
# A list of rules defining target criteria for VKS clusters.
rules:
- apiGroup: "cluster.x-k8s.io"
kind: "Cluster"
# Required. Specific namespaces on the Supervisor to monitor.
namespaces:
nameSelector: ["vks-development-ns", "vks-staging-ns"]
# Optional. Filter targets by specific name.
nameSelector: ["vks-cluster-01"]
# Optional. Standard Kubernetes label selector.
labelSelector:
matchLabels:
environment: dev
# Optional. Common Expression Language (CEL) selector.
celSelector:
matchExpressions:
- "object.metadata.name.startsWith('vks-dev-')"
# Config template to apply to the auto-generated ManagedEntity and ArgoCD secret.
config:
# Additional labels for the resulting Argo CD cluster secret.
secretLabels:
vks-management: "auto"
# Additional annotations for the resulting Argo CD cluster secret.
secretAnnotations:
security-level: "internal"
# Argo CD AppProject to associate with. Default is "default".
argoCDProject: "default"
# HTTP/HTTPS proxy URL for cluster communication.
proxy: "http://proxy.example.com:8080"
# Disables automatic compression for requests to the cluster.
disableCompression: false
2. Apply the manifest to deploy the policy.
bash kubectl apply -f <policy namea> -n argocd-1

Behavior on Policy Deletion
If you delete an resource, the controller does not delete the resources
EntityManagementPolicy ManagedEntity
that it created. The resources remain in the system to prevent production application disruption. The
ManagedEntity
controller automatically sets the managed-by annotations and labels to an empty string, marking them as unmanaged. If
another active policy is available, that policy takes over management of the clusters.

spec.enabled: false
actively monitor target deletions. If a target cluster is deleted, a disabled policy still triggers the automatic deletion of its
corresponding to prevent orphaned resources.

system
When using the upstream cluster add command to register a vSphere Namespace keep the

Argo CD Custom Resource Reference
The Argo CD resource is a Kubernetes Custom Resource (CRD) that describes the desired state for a given Argo CD
instance and allows for the configuration of the components that make up an Argo CD instance.
When the Argo CD Supervisor Service watches a Argo CD resource being created or updated, the components are
provisioned by using Kubernetes resources. When something changes on an existing Argo CD resource, the Argo CD
Supervisor Service starts to reconfigure the Argo CD instance to ensure its actual state matches the desired state. The
components consisting of an Argo CD Instance are the same as Argo CD upstream.
Since Argo CD Supervisor Service is an operator, it controls certain resources. If you directly modify these resources
without interacting with Agro CD spec, the configurations will be reverted back by Argo CD Supervisor Service. See the
table from below to get familiar with what kinds of resources that you can directly manipulate.
Check the Argo CD API Reference for the most up-to-date information about resources and operations what you can use
with the Argo CD service.
State Reconciliation Behavior
The operator actively monitors and reconciles resources based on their control level. The following table describes each
control level.
Control Level Behavior
Yes The operator actively monitors and reconciles the resource. If you
directly edit the resource, the operator automatically reverts your
changes to match the state defined in the custom resource spec.
No The operator initializes the resource with default values
upon creation. You can safely edit the resource directly after
deployment.
Partially The operator controls and overwrites only specific critical keys
synced from the custom resource. Other keys are preserved on
update.
Warning:
Do not directly edit resources that are marked as Yes or Partially controlled. The operator reconciliation loop
automatically reverts your changes.

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
ManagedEntity Custom Resource Manifest Example
apiVersion: argocd-service.vsphere.vmware.com/v1alpha1
kind: ManagedEntity
metadata:
name: corporate-vks-dev-reg
namespace: argocd-1 # The namespace where your ArgoCD is deployed
spec:
# The reference to the target cluster
targetRef:
apiGroup: "cluster.x-k8s.io"
kind: "Cluster"
name: "vks-cluster-01" # VKS cluster object name
namespace: "test-1" # Hosting vSphere namespace where the VKS cluster resides
# Custom display name for the cluster inside ArgoCD.
# Defaults to "&lt;cluster-name&gt;-&lt;namespace&gt;" (e.g., vks-cluster-01-test-1) if omitted.
clusterName: corporate-vks-development
# Restrict ArgoCD to manage only these specific namespaces inside the target VKS cluster.
# If left empty/nil, ArgoCD is granted access to manage all namespaces in the VKS cluster.
namespaces:
- app-dev-01
- app-dev-02
# Custom labels applied to the generated Argo CD cluster secret.
secretLabels:
environment: development
region: primary
# Custom annotations applied to the generated Argo CD cluster secret.
secretAnnotations:
security-policy: standard
# The ArgoCD AppProject to associate this cluster with. Defaults to "default".
argoCDProject: "default"
# Optional HTTP/HTTPS proxy URL for cluster API communication.
proxy: "http://proxy.example.com:8080"
# Disables automatic GZip compression for API requests to the cluster.
disableCompression: false
EntityManagementPolicy Custom Resource Manifest Example
apiVersion: argocd-service.vsphere.vmware.com/v1alpha1
kind: EntityManagementPolicy
metadata:
name: primary-vks-policy
namespace: argocd-1 # The namespace where your ArgoCD instance is deployed
spec:
# Enable or disable the policy. Default is true.
enabled: true
# A list of matching rules. A target VKS cluster is registered if it matches ANY rule in the list.
rules:
# Rule 1: Matches VKS clusters in development or staging namespaces with specific label
- apiGroup: "cluster.x-k8s.io"
kind: "Cluster"
VMware by Broadcom 442

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
# Required. List of Supervisor namespaces to monitor. Minimum length 1.
namespaces:
nameSelector: ["vks-development-ns", "vks-staging-ns"]
# Optional standard Kubernetes label selector.
labelSelector:
matchLabels:
environment: dev
tier: backend
# Rule 2: Matches VKS clusters using CEL expression and specific names
- apiGroup: "cluster.x-k8s.io"
kind: "Cluster"
namespaces:
nameSelector: ["vks-prod-ns"]
# Optional list of specific cluster names on the Supervisor to match.
nameSelector: ["vks-prod-cluster-01", "vks-prod-cluster-02"]
# Optional Common Expression Language (CEL) selector evaluated against the cluster resource.
# The cluster resource is mapped to the 'object' variable.
celSelector:
matchExpressions:
- "object.metadata.name.startsWith('vks-prod-')"
- "object.metadata.name != 'vks-prod-temp-cluster'"
# Configuration template to inject into the auto-generated ManagedEntity and ArgoCD secret.
config:
# Custom labels to apply to the auto-generated Argo CD cluster secret.
secretLabels:
vks-management: "auto"
managed-by-policy: "primary-vks-policy"
# Custom annotations to apply to the auto-generated Argo CD cluster secret.
secretAnnotations:
security-level: "high"
# Argo CD AppProject to associate with. Defaults to "default".
argoCDProject: "default"
# Optional HTTP/HTTPS proxy URL for cluster API communication.
proxy: "http://proxy.example.com:8080"
# Disables automatic GZip compression for API requests.
disableCompression: false
