VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
Installing Contour as a Supervisor Service
You can install Contour as a Supervisor Service in the Supervisors environment. Contour is an open-source Ingress
controller for Kubernetes that deploys the Envoy proxy as a reverse proxy and load balancer.
You can use Contour as an Ingress controller for your applications. You can also use it as a dependency for other
Supervisor Services, for example, Harbor. When you use it with Harbor, Contour provides external access to the Harbor
registry through Ingress.
When deployed as a Supervisor Service, Contour provides the following capabilities and features:
• An open-source Ingress controller based on the Envoy proxy.
• Dynamic configuration updates without service disruption.
• Integration with Harbor and other Supervisor Service that require Ingress.
• A lightweight footprint optimized for Kubernetes environments.
When deployed, the Contour Supervisor Service creates vSphere Pods in the namespace provisioned for the service.
These vSphere Pods are required for Contour operation.
Install Contour as a Supervisor Service
You can install Contour as a Supervisor Service in the Supervisors environment. Once Contour is installed, you can use it
as an Ingress controller for your applications. Contour can also be used for running Harbor as a Supervisor Service.
• Verify that you have upgraded to vCenter 8.0a or higher. Contour Supervisor Service is supported with vCenter 8.0a
and higher.
• Verify that you have the Manage Supervisor Services privilege on the vCenter system where you add the services.
1. Log in to support.broadcom.com, search for vSphere Supervisor Services, and download an appropriate version of
Contour from the vSphere Supervisor Services page.
You download the following yml files:
• x.xx.x - Service definition file for Contour. This file is a manifest that tells the
contour-service- .yml
Supervisor how to define the Contour service within the environment. It contains the metadata, version
compatibility, structure of the Contour service, and other information.
• - Configuration or data values file.
contour-data-values.yml

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
2. In the vSphere Client go to Supervisor Management, and select Services.
3. Deploy the service operator of Contour by clicking Add New Service and uploading the
contour-
x.xx.x service definition file.
service- .yml
Once the Contour operator is registered, it appears in the Services tab:

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
Installing and Configuring the Local Consumption Interface
For vSphere Foundation DevOps users who do not have access to VCF Automation, the Local Consumption Interface
provides an interface within the vSphere Client that allows creation of VMs, VKS Clusters, and Volumes.
The Local Consumption Interface can be launched as a standalone application, allowing you to grant access to the
interface to users who do not have vSphere Client access.
For more information on using the Local Consumption Interface to deploy workloads, see Building Cloud Applications.
Install the Local Consumption Interface
You can install the Local Consumption Interface as a Supervisor service.
Ensure that you have the Supervisor Admin role before installing the Local Consumption Interface.
Beginning with VCF 9.1, the Local Consumption Interface is a Core Supervisor service, and is installed when the
Supervisor is enabled. You do not need to perform the following steps in VCF 9.1 or later.
1. Using the vSphere Client, log in to vCenter as a Supervisor Admin.
2. Download the manifest file from the Broadcom Support Portal at https://support.broadcom.com/group/
ecx/productfiles?subFamily=vSphere%20Supervisor%20Services&displayGroup=Local%20Consumption
%20Interface&release=9.0.0&os=&servicePk=&language=EN.
3. In the vSphere Client go to Supervisor Management, and select Services.
4. Deploy the Local Consumption Interface by clicking Add New Service and uploading the
lci-svs-9.0.0.yml
manifest file.
The Consumption Interface tile appears in the Services tab.
5. In the Consumption Interface tile, select Actions > Manage Service.
6. Select the Supervisor on which you want to install the Local Consumption Interface, and click Next.
7. On the review page, click Finish.
No additional input is required for the YAML service configuration.
After the service installation finishes, a banner appears indicating that a vCenter plugin has been installed.
Upgrade the Local Consumption Interface
Newer versions of the Local Consumption Interface are released periodically.
The upgrade process for the Local Consumption Interface varies depending on the version you are starting from.
Follow the upgrade procedure for your version of the Local Consumption Interface.
• If you are starting with version 1.0.x of the Local Consumption Interface and want to upgrade to a later version,
uninstall the Local Consumption Interface, and then install a 9.x version by following the instructions in Install the Local
Consumption Interface.
• If you are starting with a 9.x version of the Local Consumption Interface and want to upgrade to a later version, add the
new version following the instructions in Add a New Version to a, and then upgrade using the instructions in Upgrade a
to a Newer Version.
Launch the Standalone Local Consumption Interface
You can launch a standalone version of the Local Consumption Interface to allow it to be used without accessing the
vSphere Client.

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
Installing and Configuring the Secret Store Service
As a VI Administrator, you can install the Secret Store service as a VCF service that spans across a region. You can also
deploy it on an individual Supervisor as a Supervisor Service.
The Secret Store service is a centralized service for managing and securing secrets in your environment. It leverages
OpenBao to provide secure secret management for workloads.
The Secret Store service integrates with the Supervisor and VKS clusters, enabling role-based access for administrators,
DevOps engineers, and application tenants. It supports Kubernetes-native APIs, enforces security standards, and
simplifies secret management.
The Secret Store service helps to manage, store, and distribute sensitive data, such as key-value pairs.
Secrets in the Secret Store service belong to a single namespace, and can be used only by workloads in that namespace.
Workload such as VM Service VMs, vSphere Pods, and pods inside VKS clusters can consume secrets created by the
Secret Store service.
Install Secret Store Service Using VCF Automation
You can install the Secret Store service through the Service Management option in the VCF Automation Provider
Management portal. You can install the service in all available and future regions or only to regions that you select. A
Secret Store instance will be installed to only one of the Supervisor instances per region, and the services configuration is
propagated to the rest of the Supervisors in the region.
1. Log in to the VCF Automation Provider Management Portal.
2. In the left navigation pane, click Service Management.
3. On the VCF Services tab, scroll down to the Not installed list of services.
4. On the Secret Store Service card, click Install.
5. Review the certificates and click Accept Certificates and Continue.
6. On the Select Deployment Scope page, select one of the options.
Option Description
Deploy to all existing regions and newly created ones Select this option to install the Secret Store service to all existing
regions and to automatically trigger the installation to all new
regions that will be created in the future.
Deploy to specific regions Install the Secret Store service only to specific regions that you
select.
7. On the Service Properties page, you can manually edit the default installation options by editing the service definition
YAML file.
a) On the left of the screen, click YAML View.
The YAML containing the installation properties is displayed.
b) Select the Edit Service Configuration toggle.
For air-gapped environments, specify the input parameter. For information, see Configure
agentInjectImage
the agentInjectImage Parameter for Air-Gapped Environments.
c) Click Save when you are done with your edits.
8. On the Review and Finalise page, review the configured service properties and click Submit.
Install and Configure Secret Store Service as a Supervisor Service
You can install Secret Store service as a Supervisor Service in the Supervisor environment.

After you install the Secret Store service, a dedicated namespace is created. Inside the namespace, several vSphere
Pods are deployed to run the service and take care of the secret management operations.
After you create a namespace, the system automatically sets up the following items:
• Authentication.
VMware by Broadcom 451

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
• Path for secret creation. Path is .
secret/data
• Default policy for the namespace. Policy name matches the namespace name, . The policy
secret/data/ns-name
gives the capability to read and list all secrets of the namespace.
• Default role that uses the default policy to enable all service accounts of the namespace to read and list secrets. The
role name matches the namespace name.
For existing namespaces, the default policy and role are created when secrets are created or listed for the first time for
that namespace.
Configure the agentInjectImage Parameter for Air-Gapped
Environments
For air-gapped environments, you must specify the agentInjectImage input parameter when installing the Secret Store
service. This parameter defines the fully qualified image path and digest for the secret store agent injector image stored in
your private registry.
1. To retrieve the image digest from your private Harbor registry, run the following command:
curl -k -X 'GET' 'https://myregistry.com/api/v2.0/projects/<PROJECT_NAME>/repositories/
secret-store-service/artifacts' -u '<Harbor_username>:<Harbor_password>'
2. In the response output, locate the image digest value.
For example,
"digest": "sha256:baad64ba84bb8a639c5a7a1aaff744bcb51b01ef8e7c9eb2b4f5d45ad71d9171"
3. Create the agentInjectImage value using the following format:
<registry>/<project>/secret-store-service@<digest>

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
Installing and Configuring the Velero Plugin for vSphere on a
Supervisor
The Velero Plugin for vSphere provides a solution for backing up and restoring workloads. Once you have the Velero
Plugin for vSphere installed and configured on a Supervisor, you can back up and restore VKS cluster workloads and
vSphere Pods. For persistent workloads, the Velero Plugin for vSphere lets you take snapshots of the persistent volumes.
Install and Configure the Velero Plugin Version 1.8.x for vSphere
Learn how to install and configure the Velero Plugin for vSphere to back up and restore workloads running on vSphere
Pods and VKS clusters.
Before You Begin
Be familiar with the following information and perform the required steps:
• These installation instructions apply only to Velero Plugin for vSphere version 1.8.0-embedded+24696422 or any
version with the 1.8 prefix. For information about installing version 1.7.x and earlier, see Install and Configure the
Velero Plugin Version 1.7.x in the vSphere Supervisor 8.0 documentaiton.
• Before installing the new Velero versions, uninstall the current Velero installation. Failing to do so might have
unintended consequences. Use the uninstall command that is described in Uninstall the Velero Plugin for vSphere.
• If you use an air-gapped environment, before following these installation instructions, perform the required steps in
Install the Velero Plugin for vSphere in an Air-Gapped Environment.
Supported Versions
Velero Plugin for vSphere Supervisor 8.x and Earlier vSphere Supervisor 9.0 and Later
1.8.0-embedded+24696422 or any version Yes Yes
with the 1.8 prefix With Supervisor version 8.0 Update 3g and
later
1.7.x and earlier Yes No
Using Velero Commands
Velero is installed in the Supervisor Service namespace. All Velero commands must specify the Velero Supervisor Service
namespace explicitly. For more details, see https://velero.io/docs/v1.16/namespace/.
If you use the following command, you can avoid specifying the namespace repeatedly.
velero client config set namespace=svc-velero-domain-c38
Where is the Velero Supervisor Service namespace.
svc-velero-domain-c38
Prerequisites
• Supervisor is activated.
• A vSphere Namespace is created and configured.
• You must be a member of the VI administrator role. See Using vCenter Roles to Assign Privileges.
• Create a Linux VM where you can run the Velero CLI. Or use an existing Linux jump host where you access
Supervisor.
• The Velero version numbers are presented as . Refer to the Velero Compatibility Matrix for the specific versions
X.Y.Z
to use, and substitute accordingly when running the commands.

Step 0 (Optional): Create a Dedicated Network for Backup and Restore Traffic
Although not required, it is recommended that for production environments you separate the backup and restore traffic
from the Supervisor control plane management network traffic.
There are two aspects to this:
• Tag the ESX hosts to support network file copy (NFC)
• Configure the backup and restore network using NSX.
To configure ESX hosts to support a dedicated network block device (NBD) transport, you add a VMkernel NIC on each
ESX host in the vSphere clusters where the Supervisor runs and set the on that NIC. When the
vSphereBackupNFC
tag is applied to the NIC type for a VMkernel adapter, backup and restore traffic goes through the
vSphereBackupNFC
selected virtual NIC.
To perform this configuration, you use the Virtual Disk Development Kit. See the Best Practices for NBD Transport in the
Virtual Disk Development Kit Programming Guide.
Note:
If the is not enabled on the VMkernel NIC, the backup and restore traffic will be not be sent
vSphereBackupNFC
on the backup and restore network, even if you configure one. If is not enabled, the traffic
vSphereBackupNFC
will travel on the vSphere management network.
Once the tag is enabled, configure the backup and restore network to use NSX by updating the
vSphereBackupNFC
existing vSphere Distributed Switch (VDS) for the cluster as follows.
1. In the vSphere Client, select Menu > Networking.
2. Select the existing VDS for the cluster.
3. Right-click the VDS and select Distributed Port Group > New Distributed Port Group.
4. Create a new Distributed Port Group named BackupRestoreNetwork.
5. Add a VMkernel adapter to the BackupRestoreNetwork Distributed Port Group.
6. Attach all the ESX hosts in the vCenter cluster where the Supervisor is enabled to the BackupRestoreNetwork
Distributed Port Group.
7. Enable the tag.
vSphereBackupNFC

For backup and restore of persistent volumes, you must provide an S3-compatible object store. Velero supports several
object store providers. See official Velero documentation.

Step 2: Install and Configure Data Manager
To facilitate backup and restore using the Velero Plugin for vSphere, you deploy one or more Data Manager VMs to move
persistent volume backup data in and out of S3-compatible object storage. Data Manager moves the volume snapshot
data from the vSphere volume to the remote durable S3-compatible storage on backup, and from remote S3-compatible
storage to a vSphere volume during restore.
Warning:
Data Manager is only functionally tested and it is not meant to work at scale and does not promise any
performance expectations. It is not meant to backup business critical applications in production.

Using the Velero Plugin with Third-Party Backup Solutions
Third-party backup solutions can use the Velero Plugin for vSphere to back up and restore VKS clusters.
The third-party solution uses the Velero Plugin to take VKS backups. But backup orchestration and workflows are handled
through the vendor’s own user interface. This approach allows third-party vendors to integrate with VKS while providing
their own backup and restore experience.
For vendor-specific implementation details, refer to the documentation provided by the third-party backup solution.

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
Configuring Encryption Management as a provider
administrator
Encryption Management is a service which grants organization administrators the ability to use encryption keys from their
own key providers for encryption of virtual machines (with or without vTPM devices) and disks in their VMware Cloud
Foundation environment.
As a provider administrator, refer to the content in this chapter to learn how to set up Encryption Management for your
organizations.
How to set up Encryption Management as a provider administrator
The Encryption Management service is pre-installed and enabled in your VMware Cloud Foundation Automation instance.
As a provider administrator, follow these steps to set up Encryption Management for organizations.
1. Register a key provider with Encryption Management
2. Publish a key provider to an organization
Once a key provider is published to an organization, the organization gains access to the Encryption Management
service.
Before you begin
Before you configure the Encryption Management service, you must first prepare your environment.
The Encryption Management service requires your VMware Cloud Foundation environment to be pre-configured. To
prepare all components in your environment, ensure that you satisfy the requirements in the following table.
Product Requirements
vCenter • A default standard key provider must be defined.
• One or more storage policies with encryption capabilities.
VCF Automation • Running version 9.1 or later.
• One or more storage classes with encryption enabled (VM
Encryption Policy) added by the provider in a region.
Key Provider • Obtain the key provider's IP address, port, proxy, and HA
settings.
• vCenter must have network connectivity to the key provider.
• Verify that the key provider is included in VMware Compatibility
Guide for Key Management Servers (KMS).
• The key provider cannot be vSphere Native Key Provider.
Register a key provider with Encryption Management
You register a key provider in the Encryption Management service and associate it with a vCenter instance.
• Obtain the IP addresses and ports of the key provider servers that you are registering. The default port is 5696.
1. Log in to the VCF Automation Provider Management UI.
2. From the side navigation bar, expand VCF Services and select Encryption.
If this is the first key provider you are registering, an introductory page is displayed.
VMware by Broadcom 463

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
3. To register a key provider, click GET STARTED or REGISTER.
4. Fill in the key provider details.
a) Enter a key provider name.
b) Optional: Enter a description.
The description is visible to organization administrators.
c) Optional: To upload an icon from your local drive, click BROWSE.
d) Enter a key provider server IP address and port.
e) Optional: To add more key provider servers, select ADD and enter the server's IP address and port.
Note:
Additional key provider servers ensure high availability of the service. The servers must share the same
encryption keys.
f) Optional: To set up a proxy, expand PROXY SETTINGS and enter the proxy address and port.
g) Click NEXT.
5. Select the vCenter instance to be associated with the key provider.
6. Click REGISTER.
You are prompted to validate and trust the certificates of the key provider servers.

VMware Cloud Foundation Service Administration and Development 9.1
Publish a key provider to an organization
To grant an organization with access to a key provider, you publish a key provider that is registered in Encryption
Management to an organization.
1. Log in to the VCF Automation Provider Management UI.
2. From the side navigation bar, expand VCF Services and select Encryption.
3. Next to a key provider, click the vertical-ellipsis icon
( ) >
PUBLISH.
4. From the list of organizations, select the ones that you want to publish the key provider to.
5. Optional: Under Name in vCenter, enter a unique name for each organization in vCenter.
If you configured a replication site, the name in the source and destination must be the same.
Note:
After you publish a key provider to your organization, you cannot change the name in vCenter.
6. Click PUBLISH.
Unpublish a key provider from an organization
If you want to revoke an organization's access to a key provider, you can unpublish the key provider from the organization.
To unpublish a key provider, your vCenter instance must be configured with a default key provider or there must be no
organization objects encrypted with the key provider you want to unpublish.
1. Log in to the VCF Automation Provider Management UI.
2. From the side navigation bar, expand VCF Services and select Encryption.
3. Click the name of the key provider that you want to unpublish.
4. Under Organizations, next to the organization name you want to unpublish the key provider from, click the vertical-
ellipsis icon
( )
and click Unpublish.
5. Move the slider to the right and click Unpublish.
The unpublish process runs in the background. The organization is revoked access to the key provider and all affected
objects are re-encrypted with the vCenter's default key provider.
Edit a key provider
You can edit a registered key provider's details and network configuration.
Important:
If you edit the network configuration of a key provider, all organizations with access to the key provider must re-
authenticate to it before they can use it again. Failure to authenticate after changing the network configuration
may prevent organizations from performing operations on existing encrypted objects and create new encrypted
ones. You are responsible of notifying your organizations about this change.

learning VMs, Kubernetes clusters, and RAG applications.
Model Runtime As an MLOps engineer, you can run LLMs paired with inference
engines as model endpoints.
Data Indexing and Retrieval As a data scientist, you can connect to and index data from
multiple sources so that you can use it in knowledge bases for
contextual search in RAG applications using the PostgreSQL
vector database of the Private AI Services instance. S
MCP Servers and Tool Gallery As an MLOps engineer, you can add data and capabilities in the
form of MCP tools available on one or more MCP servers for use
in agents and AI applications.
Private AI Services provides MCP integration that is based on tool
calling. MCP prompts, sampling, or resources are not applicable to
the use cases Private AI Services is designed for.
Agent Buider As an application developer, you can create an agent that uses
running models from Model Runtime with context from MCP tools
and knowledge bases in Data Indexing and Retrieval and prompt
tuning that you can access over an API.
Observability As an MLOps engineer or application developer, you can perform
monitoring and diagnostics of models, which are used in agents, in
observability platforms like Grafana to track the health, quality, and
behavior of AI applications.
Installing and Configuring Private AI Services
For more information about installing and configuring Private AI Services in a namespace, see Setup Workloflow for
Private AI Services and Installing and Configuring Private AI Services in the VMware Private AI Foundation with NVIDIA
documentation.
